zones.label: Georgian Bay & Northern Boreal
zones.blurb: Killarney's pink granite and Hwy 129's boreal canyon set the tone before the real distances begin.
tips: Top off fuel in Thessalon — services thin out fast heading north on Hwy 129.
Killarney's Herbert Fisheries is worth timing lunch around.
Crown-land pull-offs north of Thessalon are free but arrive with daylight to scout a spot.

safety.cellCoverage: Patchy once off Hwy 400/17 onto Hwy 129 — download offline maps first.
safety.note: Standard 911 coverage on the main highways; gaps on Hwy 129 itself.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Parry Sound
pois.note: Fuel and diesel just off Hwy 400 as you enter Parry Sound heading north.

pois.name: Coniston Esso
pois.note: Esso stop on Hwy 17 E on Sudbury's eastern edge, good last-fuel before Espanola.

pois.name: Espanola Esso (331 Hwy 17 W)
pois.note: Esso/Circle K right on Hwy 17 through Espanola, easy pull-in for gas and snacks.

pois.name: Blind River Esso (498 Causley St)
pois.note: Reliable fuel stop on Hwy 17 in Blind River before heading north on Hwy 129.
pois.address: 498 Causley St, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: Thessalon Esso
pois.note: Last major fuel in Thessalon before the long stretch north on Hwy 129.

pois.name: Herbert Fisheries
pois.note: Iconic lakeside fish-and-chips shack in Killarney village, a must-stop road-trip classic.

pois.name: Loretta's Bakery & Marketplace
pois.note: Well-loved bakery/market just south of Parry Sound off Hwy 400, great pies and baked goods to go.
pois.address: 1297 Lake Joseph Rd, Seguin, ON P2A 2W8

pois.name: French River Trading Post
pois.note: Historic Hwy 69 roadside outpost with restaurant, gifts, and a scenic French River bridge view.

pois.name: The Little Brew Cafe
pois.note: Small-town cafe in Massey for coffee and a bite between Espanola and Blind River.
pois.address: 365 Imperial St S, Massey, ON P0P 1P0

pois.name: A Touch of Home Bakery
pois.note: Locally loved bakery in Blind River, good for treats before the Hwy 129 push north.
pois.address: 10 Woodward Ave, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: George Lake Campground, Killarney Provincial Park
pois.note: Reservable drive-in campground with showers, good base for hiking The Crack, RV-friendly sites.

pois.name: Chutes Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Riverside campground right in Massey with waterfall trails steps from the sites.
pois.address: 650 Imperial Street North, Massey, ON P0P 1P0
pois.hours: Seasonal: May 15–Oct 13, park office hours vary — call ahead

pois.name: Mississagi Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Remote, quiet park north of Elliot Lake off Hwy 639, good backcountry-feel car camping.
pois.address: Off Hwy 639 north of Elliot Lake, ON (admin/mailing: c/o Chutes PP, 650 Imperial St N, Massey, ON P0P 1P0)
pois.hours: Seasonal: May 15–Oct 13, park office hours vary — call ahead

pois.name: Thessalon Lakeside Park Campground
pois.note: In-town campground on Lake Huron shoreline in Thessalon, easy overnight before heading north.

pois.name: Crown Land Camping, Hwy 129 / Mississagi River corridor
pois.note: Free dispersed Crown-land pull-offs along Hwy 129 north of Thessalon, popular with van/RV boondockers.

pois.name: The Crack Trail
pois.note: Killarney's signature strenuous hike to a dramatic quartzite ridge with panoramic views.

pois.name: Chikanishing Trail
pois.note: Easy loop along pink granite Georgian Bay shoreline, great short leg-stretcher stop.

pois.name: Bridal Veil Falls (Kagawong)
pois.note: Popular walk-behind waterfall on Manitoulin Island, worth the short detour from Espanola.

pois.name: Chutes Provincial Park Waterfalls
pois.note: Short riverside trail past cascading falls right off Hwy 17 in Massey, easy scenic stop.

pois.name: Mississagi River Valley Viewpoint (Hwy 129)
pois.note: One of Ontario's most scenic drives, a winding canyon-like valley with pull-off lookouts.

pois.name: Potholes Provincial Nature Reserve
pois.note: Glacial pothole rock formations near Elliot Lake, a quick offbeat nature stop.

pois.name: Shell Parry Sound
pois.note: Convenient in-town fill-up on Bowes Street before joining Hwy 400 north out of Parry Sound.
pois.address: 116 Bowes Street, Parry Sound, ON P2A 2L2

pois.name: Petro-Pass Truck Stop (Regent St)
pois.note: 24-hour truck stop with diesel, restrooms and a convenience store — a reliable overnight fuel stop on the Sudbury bypass.

pois.name: Esso Sudbury (Regent St S)
pois.note: 24-hour Esso with an attached car wash and auto repair bay on the main Regent Street strip through south Sudbury.
pois.address: 1813 Regent St S, Sudbury, ON P3E 3Z7

pois.name: Shell Massey
pois.note: Some of the cleanest bathrooms on Hwy 17 and often the last station reliably open before the stretch west toward Spanish.
pois.address: 465 Sauble St E, Massey, ON P0P 1P0

pois.name: Broken Canoe Trading Post
pois.note: First Nation-run full-service station open around the clock — a useful backup if the in-town Esso is busy.
pois.address: 7 West St, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0 (Mississauga First Nation #8, ~10.5 km SSW of town)

pois.name: Iron Bridge Service Station
pois.note: Small-town fuel and coffee stop roughly midway between Blind River and Thessalon.
pois.address: 1100 Hwy 17 W, Iron Bridge, ON P0R 1H0

pois.name: Canadian Tire Gas+ Elliot Lake
pois.note: Pump-and-go gas with the Canadian Tire auto centre next door for a quick tire or battery check.
pois.address: 50 Hillside Drive S, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 1M7

pois.name: Esso Elliot Lake
pois.note: 24-hour fuel with an attached car wash near the Hwy 108 entrance to town.
pois.address: 225 Hwy 108 N, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 2T1

pois.name: Petro-Canada Cardlock (Killarney)
pois.note: Commercial cardlock fuel that may need a Petro-Canada fleet card — treat as a backup, not a guaranteed public pump, in fuel-scarce Killarney.
pois.address: 437 Finlay St E, Killarney, ON P0M 2A0
pois.hours: 24/7 self-serve (fleet card typically required) — call ahead

pois.name: Point Grondine Trading Post
pois.note: First Nation gas bar directly on Hwy 637, useful for topping off on the spur road to or from Killarney.
pois.address: Hwy 637, Point Grondine First Nation, ON (between the French River area and Killarney)

pois.name: Happy Grillmore's
pois.note: Chip-stand classic near the Hwy 17/6 junction serving local whitefish and pickerel fish & chips.

pois.name: Cortina's
pois.note: Sit-down Italian option in downtown Espanola for a break from highway fast food.

pois.name: The Pier Sports Bar & Restaurant
pois.note: Waterfront pub right on Causley Street, an easy walk from the Blind River Esso.
pois.address: 1 Causley Street, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: On The River Restaurant
pois.note: Riverside sit-down dining a short drive off Hwy 17 in Blind River.
pois.address: 303 Eldorado Road, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: Sinton Tavern
pois.note: Family-run pizza, wings and pub food on Thessalon's Main Street — closed Mondays, so plan around it.
pois.hours: Mon closed, Tue–Fri 10am–8pm (Thu to 10pm), Sat 1pm–9pm, Sun closed

pois.name: FireSide Classic Grill
pois.note: Locally loved breakfast-through-dinner grill in Elliot Lake, good for a real sit-down meal off the highway.
pois.address: 14 Oakland Blvd, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 2T1
pois.hours: Daily, open until 9pm — call for opening time

pois.name: Deluxe Hamburgers
pois.note: 56-year-old classic drive-in on Regent Street — a Sudbury institution for burgers and fries.

pois.name: Henry's Fish Restaurant
pois.note: Floating fish-and-chips restaurant on Georgian Bay reached only by water taxi from the downtown Parry Sound docks — a fun detour, but call ahead for pickup.
pois.address: Water-taxi access from the Government Dock, downtown Parry Sound, ON
pois.hours: Seasonal (summer); boat pickup by call — hours not published, call ahead

pois.name: Oastler Lake Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Full-service provincial campground minutes from Parry Sound with showers, a dump station and a boat launch.
pois.address: 380 Oastler Park Drive, Seguin, ON P2A 2W8

pois.name: Grundy Lake Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Popular family campground with smooth granite swimming shores, a short detour off Hwy 400/69 south of Parry Sound.

pois.name: Windy Lake Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Electrical and non-electrical sites with showers, about 45 minutes west of Sudbury via Hwy 144.
pois.address: 1 Old Cartier Road, Levack, ON P0M 2C0

pois.name: Halfway Lake Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Large, less-crowded campground roughly an hour north of Sudbury on Hwy 144, with over a dozen lakes to explore.
pois.address: Hwy 144, 26 km north of Cartier, ON P0M 2C0

pois.name: Fairbank Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Small spring-fed lake with a sandy beach, half an hour west of Sudbury — good for a quick swim break.

pois.name: Serpent River Campground
pois.note: Private riverside campground with pull-through big-rig sites and a pool, roughly midway between Blind River and Elliot Lake.
pois.hours: Seasonal — hours not published, call ahead

pois.name: Westview Trailer Park
pois.note: Municipal campground on Elliot Lake itself with full hookups and a boat launch, walkable to town amenities (ask for ext. 2406 to book).

pois.name: South Bay Park
pois.note: Private campground on Dunlop Lake north of Elliot Lake with canoe/kayak/paddleboat rentals — reservations required.
pois.address: 101 South Bay Rd, Elliot Lake, ON

pois.name: Bell Lake Access Point Backcountry Camping (Killarney PP)
pois.note: Canoe-in backcountry gateway on Hwy 637 for Killarney's interior campsites and the Silver Peak/La Cloche Silhouette Trail.
pois.address: Bell Lake Rd off Hwy 637, Killarney Provincial Park, ON
pois.hours: Seasonal backcountry access, permits via park office — call ahead

pois.name: A.Y. Jackson Lookout & Onaping High Falls
pois.note: Wheelchair-accessible lookout over a 55-metre waterfall that Group of Seven painter A.Y. Jackson made famous — an easy detour off Hwy 144 north of Sudbury.
pois.address: Hwy 144, ~5 km north of Dowling, Sudbury, ON

pois.name: Silver Peak
pois.note: Highest point in Killarney Provincial Park (539m) with sweeping views over white quartzite ridges — a serious day hike or canoe-in trip, not a casual stroll.
pois.address: Killarney Provincial Park (La Cloche Mountains), accessed via Bell Lake or George Lake trailheads, Killarney, ON
pois.hours: Open year-round; backcountry permit required for overnight trips

pois.name: La Cloche Silhouette Trail
pois.note: 78km backcountry loop through Killarney's white quartzite mountains — for experienced backpackers only, but sections make good day hikes.
pois.address: Trailhead at George Lake day-use area, Killarney Provincial Park, ON
pois.hours: Open year-round; backcountry camping permit required

pois.name: Helenbar Lake Lookout Trail
pois.note: Moderate 7km hike to a 130m-high lookout over the surrounding hills and boulder erratics.
pois.address: Mississagi Provincial Park, off Hwy 639 north of Elliot Lake, ON

pois.name: Flack Lake Nature Trail
pois.note: Easy 0.8km interpretive trail past old logging-camp remnants and interesting rock formations — a good stretch-the-legs stop.
pois.address: Mississagi Provincial Park, off Hwy 639 north of Elliot Lake, ON

pois.name: Grundy Lake Beaches & Gut Lake Trail
pois.note: Smooth granite swimming shores and a moderate loop trail across Canadian Shield terrain and wetlands draining into Georgian Bay.

pois.name: Fairbank Lake Beach & Trails
pois.note: Crystal-clear spring-fed lake with a sandy beach — an easy, kid-friendly swim stop west of Sudbury.

pois.name: Halfway Lake Hawk Ridge Trail
pois.note: Network of hiking trails through a dozen-plus lakes in a quieter, less-visited provincial park north of Sudbury.
pois.address: Hwy 144, 26 km north of Cartier, ON P0M 2C0

pois.name: Comfort Inn Parry Sound
pois.note: Chain hotel right on Bowes Street near the Hwy 400 interchange, a reliable first- or last-night stop.
pois.address: 120 Bowes St, Parry Sound, ON P2A 2L2

pois.name: Massey Motel
pois.note: Recently renovated 16-room motel directly on Hwy 17 through Massey, close to Chutes Provincial Park.
pois.address: Sauble Street West, Massey, ON P0P 1P0

pois.name: Goodman's Motel
pois.note: Budget motel right on Hwy 17 at the Hwy 6 junction into Espanola.

pois.name: North Shore Wayside Inn
pois.note: Budget motel at the Hwy 17/Wellington Ave corner in Blind River.
pois.address: Hwy 17 & Wellington Ave, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: Old Mill Motel
pois.note: Pet-friendly budget motel a five-minute walk from Lake Huron in Blind River.
pois.address: 10 Martin Street, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: Hampton Inn by Hilton Elliot Lake
pois.note: Modern chain hotel on Hwy 108 at the entrance to Elliot Lake, a solid base before or after the Hwy 129/Mississagi boreal stretch.
pois.address: 279 Highway 108 North, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 2S9

pois.name: Sportsman's Inn
pois.note: Waterfront inn on the Killarney Channel with guest access to sister-property Killarney Mountain Lodge's pool, sauna and gym.

pois.name: Killarney Mountain Lodge
pois.note: Historic resort on Georgian Bay with cabins and suites, dining and canoe/kayak/bike rentals for exploring Killarney.

pois.name: Moonlight Inn and Suites
pois.note: Motel near the Kingsway/Hwy 17 in Sudbury, a practical overnight stop entering or leaving the city.

pois.name: West Parry Sound Health Centre
pois.note: 90-bed acute-care hospital with a 24/7 emergency department — the first major hospital heading north from cottage country.
pois.address: 6 Albert St, Parry Sound, ON P2A 3A4

pois.name: Health Sciences North
pois.note: Major regional hospital and trauma centre in Sudbury — the largest, best-equipped ER on this entire corridor.
pois.address: 41 Ramsey Lake Rd, Greater Sudbury, ON P3E 5J1

pois.name: Espanola Regional Hospital and Health Centre
pois.note: Small hospital with an emergency department, useful before the longer gap west toward Blind River.

pois.name: Blind River District Health Centre (North Shore Health Network)
pois.note: North Shore Health Network hospital site with an emergency department serving the Blind River area.
pois.address: 525 Causley St, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: North Shore Health Network – Thessalon Hospital Site
pois.note: Small rural hospital that can assess and stabilize emergencies before transfer to a larger centre.
pois.hours: Emergency Dept hours vary — call ahead (small rural site, complex cases transferred to Blind River or Sault Ste. Marie)

pois.name: St. Joseph's General Hospital Elliot Lake
pois.note: Community hospital with an emergency department serving Elliot Lake and the Hwy 129/Mississagi corridor.
pois.address: 70 Spine Rd, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 1X2

pois.name: Manitoulin Health Centre – Mindemoya Site
pois.note: Hospital serving a Manitoulin Island side-trip off this corridor (e.g. Kagawong/Bridal Veil Falls) — verify it's open before counting on it.
pois.hours: Emergency Dept — this site has had temporary closures (e.g. infrastructure issues); call ahead to confirm status before relying on it

pois.name: DRUGStore Pharmacy
pois.note: Independent pharmacy on Espanola's main commercial strip for prescriptions and basic first-aid supplies.

pois.name: Shoppers Drug Mart (Parry Sound)
pois.note: Full-service pharmacy on Bowes Street for prescriptions and travel health needs before heading north.

pois.name: Shoppers Drug Mart (Elliot Lake)
pois.note: Pharmacy for restocking prescriptions before or after the Hwy 129 boreal stretch north of town.
pois.address: 220 Ontario St, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 1Y5
pois.hours: Daily, open until 8pm — call for opening time

pois.name: Valu-Mart Pharmacy
pois.note: Grocery-store pharmacy on Causley Street, open evenings later than most small-town options.
pois.address: 105 Causley Street, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: Georgian Automotive
pois.note: Four-bay shop in downtown Parry Sound with night-drop service; arranges 24-hour towing through a local partner.
pois.address: 150 Louisa Street, Parry Sound, ON P2A 3C1
pois.hours: Mon–Fri 8am–5pm, closed weekends, night drop available

pois.name: OK Tire & Auto Service (Parry Sound)
pois.note: Full mechanical service and tire sales on Joseph Street, a good pre-trip vehicle-check stop.
pois.address: 21 Joseph Street, Parry Sound, ON P2A 2G3

pois.name: Guy's Auto Service & Glass
pois.note: General repair, windshields and MTO safety inspections in Espanola.

pois.name: Bruno's Auto Repairs (NAPA Autopro)
pois.note: Family-run NAPA Autopro shop serving Blind River for over 40 years, covering brakes, suspension and general repairs.
pois.address: 290 Leacock St, Blind River, ON P0R 1B0

pois.name: Thessalon Automotive
pois.note: Warranty-approved full-service shop on Thessalon's Main Street with night-drop for early starts.

pois.name: OK Tire Elliot Lake
pois.note: Tire specialist and general auto repair, a good option before or after the remote Hwy 129 stretch.
pois.address: 9 Perini Road, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 2T1

pois.name: Choice Tire & Repair Centre
pois.note: Second Elliot Lake tire and repair option, also serving Blind River and Spanish.
pois.address: 6F Oakland Blvd, Elliot Lake, ON P5A 2T1

pois.name: Parry Sound Auto Towing & Wreckers
pois.note: 24-hour towing partner for the Parry Sound area — worth saving before heading into the remote stretch north.
pois.address: Parry Sound, ON (dispatch — mobile 24-hour towing service)

zones.label: Lake Superior North Shore
zones.blurb: The most scenic and most remote stretch of the whole route — Hwy 17 hugging the lake through Pukaskwa, Wawa, and Sault Ste. Marie.
tips: Fuel up in Wawa or White River — the White River-to-Marathon leg is long with few services.
Agawa Rock Pictographs closes in high wind/wave — check conditions before the short exposed trail.
Book Hattie Cove (Pukaskwa) ahead in shoulder season; it's the park's only frontcountry campground.

safety.cellCoverage: Long dead zones between Sault Ste. Marie and Thunder Bay — tell someone your plan.
safety.note: This is bear country — standard food storage discipline at all campsites.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (Great Northern Rd)
pois.note: Large fuel stop on the main commercial strip entering Sault Ste. Marie from the east.

pois.name: Circle K / Esso (Hwy 17 & Hwy 101 Junction)
pois.note: Fuel and snacks at the junction where Hwy 101 to Chapleau meets Hwy 17 in Wawa.

pois.name: Albert's & Son's Husky
pois.note: Long-standing Husky truck stop on Hwy 17, a key fuel stop in remote White River.

pois.name: Petro-Canada Marathon
pois.note: Roadside fuel stop on Hwy 17 as it passes Marathon, before the long stretch to Nipigon.

pois.name: Husky Travel Centre
pois.note: Full-service truck stop with diesel, showers and restaurant at the Hwy 17/11 split.
pois.address: 1120 Alloy Drive, Thunder Bay, ON P7B 6C5

pois.name: Voyageurs' Lodge & Cookhouse
pois.note: Popular lakeside restaurant and lodge right on Hwy 17, known for hearty comfort food.
pois.nearTown: Batchawana Bay, ON (near Sault Ste. Marie)
pois.address: Hwy 17 North, Batchawana Bay, ON P0S 1A0

pois.name: Kinniwabi Pines Restaurant
pois.note: Long-running family restaurant on Hwy 17 just south of Wawa, a classic road-trip stop.

pois.name: A&W White River
pois.note: Reliable quick-service burger stop on Hwy 17 in the self-proclaimed 'coldest spot in Canada'.

pois.name: Rossport Inn
pois.note: Historic inn and dining room in the scenic fishing village of Rossport, just off Hwy 17.

pois.name: Hoito Restaurant
pois.note: Iconic century-old Finnish restaurant in Thunder Bay, famous for all-day pancake breakfasts.
pois.address: 314 Bay Street, Thunder Bay, ON P7B 1A1

pois.name: Hattie Cove Campground
pois.note: Pukaskwa National Park's only frontcountry campground, with RV sites and Lake Superior access.
pois.address: Hwy 627 (13 km south of Hwy 17), Pukaskwa National Park, ON

pois.name: Agawa Bay Campground
pois.note: Large sandy-beach campground in Lake Superior Provincial Park, RV-friendly with a scenic shoreline.

pois.name: Rabbit Blanket Lake Campground
pois.note: Quieter inland campground near the north end of Lake Superior Provincial Park, close to Wawa.

pois.name: Neys Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Scenic Lake Superior beachfront campground with RV sites, west of Marathon on Hwy 17.

pois.name: Rainbow Falls Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Two-campground park on Whitesand Lake near Rossport, a good overnight stop before Thunder Bay.
pois.address: 1004 Highway 17, Terrace Bay, ON (Whitesand Lake Campground, north side of Hwy 17)

pois.name: Wawa Goose
pois.note: The giant roadside Canada goose statue, an essential photo-op landmark at Wawa's welcome centre.

pois.name: Agawa Rock Pictographs
pois.note: Short but exposed trail to Ojibwe rock paintings on a cliff face above Lake Superior; caution in wind/waves.

pois.name: Old Woman Bay
pois.note: Sweeping sand-and-rock beach beneath tall cliffs, one of the most photographed views on Hwy 17.

pois.name: Southern Headland / Coastal Hiking Trail
pois.note: Easy loop trail from Hattie Cove over rocky headlands with classic Pukaskwa coastline views.

pois.name: Terry Fox Memorial and Lookout
pois.note: Statue and viewpoint overlooking Lake Superior and the Sleeping Giant, marking Fox's Marathon of Hope.

pois.name: Kakabeka Falls
pois.note: Dramatic 40 m waterfall on the Kaministiquia River with boardwalk viewing platforms, west of Thunder Bay.
pois.hours: Day-use year-round; Visitor Centre open mid-May–Thanksgiving weekend

pois.name: Agawa Crafts Esso
pois.note: First Nations-owned rest stop with gas, a convenience store, café and gift shops right on the highway north of Sault Ste. Marie.
pois.address: 12502 Hwy 17 N, Batchawana Bay, ON P0S 1A0

pois.name: Esso (Pinewood Drive)
pois.note: Second fuel option in Wawa if the Circle K/Esso junction station is busy or closed.

pois.name: SPG Swipe Pump & Go (Mission Rd)
pois.note: Unstaffed pay-at-pump station useful for topping up after hours in Wawa.

pois.name: Fertengiger's Gas & Variety
pois.note: The only fuel stop actually in the village of Rossport, important given how thin services are between Schreiber and Nipigon.

pois.name: Canco Gas
pois.note: Highway-side station with a convenience store, car wash and restaurant for a full pit stop in Terrace Bay.

pois.name: Ultramar (Kingsway)
pois.note: Fuel stop in downtown Schreiber, one of several small stations worth knowing in case another is closed.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (ON-17)
pois.note: Petro-Canada with a convenience store and EV charging station at the east end of Nipigon.

pois.name: Husky/Esso (Hwy 11-17)
pois.note: 24-hour fuel and full-service stop right at the Hwy 11/17 split, useful for a late arrival or early departure from Nipigon.

pois.name: Red Rock Indian Band Gas Bar
pois.note: Full-service First Nations-owned station with a convenience store and restaurant on the Trans-Canada corridor near Nipigon.

pois.name: Travelodge Esso
pois.note: Gas station attached to the Travelodge on the south side of Hwy 17 through Marathon.

pois.name: SPG Marathon
pois.note: Gas bar with an attached convenience store and Robin's Drive Thru in Marathon.

pois.name: North of 17 Restaurant
pois.note: Hockey-memorabilia-decorated chophouse and small-town diner favourite in downtown Wawa.

pois.name: Crystal Beach Roadhouse
pois.note: Roadhouse-style stop directly on Hwy 17 through Marathon.

pois.name: Marino's Restaurant Lounge
pois.note: Long-standing family restaurant and lounge on the highway through Marathon.

pois.name: Red Dog Inn
pois.note: Family-style breakfast-through-dinner stop near Simcoe Plaza on Hwy 17 in Terrace Bay.
pois.hours: Serves breakfast, lunch and dinner — call ahead for exact hours

pois.name: Golden Rail
pois.note: Roadside chip stand and gas-bar combo right on Hwy 17 through Schreiber.

pois.name: Nipigon Esso Restaurant
pois.note: Gas-station diner combo for a quick sit-down meal while fuelling up in Nipigon.

pois.name: Stillwater Grill & Pizza
pois.note: Family restaurant with pizza, burgers, fish and gluten-free options in Nipigon.

pois.name: Ducky's Diner
pois.note: Classic diner stop on the Trans-Canada Highway in Nipigon.

pois.name: Swiss Chalet
pois.note: Reliable sit-down chain option on Great Northern Road for a last proper meal before heading into the remote stretch north of the Sault.
pois.address: 332 Great Northern Rd, Sault Ste. Marie, ON P6A 5K9

pois.name: NewBurgers
pois.note: Quick-serve burgers on Great Northern Road, convenient right before joining Hwy 17 north.
pois.address: 371 Great Northern Rd, Sault Ste. Marie, ON P6B 4Z8

pois.name: Pancake Bay Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Huge 3km white-sand-beach campground right on Hwy 17, the last big campground before Lake Superior Provincial Park heading north.
pois.nearTown: Batchawana Bay, ON (near Sault Ste. Marie)
pois.address: 12729 Highway 17 North, Batchawana Bay, ON P0S 1A0

pois.name: Naturally Superior Adventures Beach Campsites
pois.note: Beach and prospector-tent camping at the mouth of the Michipicoten River, run by the same outfitter as Rock Island Lodge.
pois.address: 10 Government Dock Rd, Wawa, ON P0S 1K0

pois.name: Obatanga Provincial Park
pois.note: Free backcountry-style camping in a genuinely remote gap between Wawa and White River, but there are zero services or drinking water.
pois.nearTown: White River, ON (between Wawa and White River)
pois.address: Hwy 17, 56 km west of Wawa / 37 km east of White River, ON
pois.hours: Non-operating park — no facilities; rustic walk-in/wilderness camping only

pois.name: Penn Lake Park Campground
pois.note: Marathon's municipal campground with serviced RV sites, showers and a beach, an easy in-town alternative to Neys.
pois.address: 61 Penn Lake Road East, Marathon, ON P0T 2E0

pois.name: Stillwater Tent and Trailer Park
pois.note: Creekside private campground right on the highway in Nipigon with pull-through RV sites.

pois.name: Sleeping Giant Provincial Park — Marie Louise Lake Campground
pois.note: 200-site campground in one of the most scenic parks on the north shore, about 45 minutes off Hwy 17/11 via Pass Lake — worth the detour near Thunder Bay.

pois.name: Kakabeka Falls Provincial Park Campground
pois.note: Convenient campground beside Ontario's famous Niagara of the North waterfall, just west of Thunder Bay.

pois.name: Rainbow Falls Provincial Park — Rossport Campground
pois.note: Smaller lakeside campground directly on Lake Superior, a quieter option than the main Whitesand Lake campground a few km east.
pois.address: Hwy 17, Rossport, ON P0T 2R0 (Rainbow Falls PP – Rossport Campground)

pois.name: Chippewa Falls
pois.note: Roadside waterfall and picnic park marking the halfway point of the Trans-Canada Highway — an easy first leg-stretcher out of the Sault.
pois.address: Hwy 17 roadside park, ~48 km north of Sault Ste. Marie, ON

pois.name: Alona Bay Scenic Lookout
pois.note: Wide pull-off with sweeping Lake Superior views and ample parking — a favourite quick photo stop for any vehicle size.
pois.address: Hwy 17 pull-off, Lake Superior Provincial Park area, ON

pois.name: Katherine Cove
pois.note: Shallow, clear turquoise water and a fine sand beach right off the highway — one of the most photographed stops in the park.
pois.address: Hwy 17, Lake Superior Provincial Park, ON P0S 1K0

pois.name: Gargantua Harbour
pois.note: Ghost-town harbour with old ranger-station remnants at the end of a rough 14km gravel road — a bigger detour but a genuine wilderness payoff.
pois.address: Gargantua Rd (14 km gravel road off Hwy 17), Lake Superior Provincial Park, ON

pois.name: Winnie the Pooh Statue (Birthplace of Winnie-the-Pooh)

pois.address: Visitor Information Centre, Hwy 17, White River, ON P0M 3G0
pois.hours: Year-round; Visitor Centre keeps seasonal hours

pois.name: Magpie High Falls (Scenic High Falls)
pois.note: A 75-foot-wide waterfall on the Magpie River just minutes from town, with an accessible viewing platform and picnic shelter.
pois.address: Off Hwy 17 south of Wawa (signed gravel access road), Wawa, ON

pois.name: White River Suspension Bridge Trail
pois.note: Demanding full-day hike ending at a swaying suspension bridge 23m above Chigamiwinigum Falls — the signature backcountry challenge of Pukaskwa.
pois.address: Trailhead at Hattie Cove, Pukaskwa National Park, ON

pois.name: Aguasabon Falls & Gorge
pois.note: Wheelchair-accessible boardwalk to a 100-foot waterfall plunging into a 2.6-billion-year-old gorge, right beside Hwy 17.
pois.address: 2 Aguasabon Gorge Rd, Terrace Bay, ON P0T 2W0

pois.name: Neys Lookout / Pic Island Overlook
pois.note: Short trail to a Group of Seven-famous view over Pic Island and Lake Superior from the former WWII POW camp site.
pois.address: Neys Provincial Park, 1004 Hwy 17, Terrace Bay, ON P0T 2W0

pois.name: Kama Cliffs Lookout
pois.note: One of the most photographed viewpoints on the North Shore — a 7.3km loop trail up to a cliff-top panorama of Nipigon Bay and Kama Point.
pois.address: Hwy 17, ~24 km east of Nipigon, ON
pois.hours: Year-round, daylight hours (winter road to lower lookout is closed)

pois.name: Rossport Lookout (Quarry Island Trail)
pois.note: 45-minute hike to a summit view over the Rossport Islands and Lake Superior, painted by Group of Seven artist Lawren Harris.
pois.address: Quarry Island, accessed by boat from Rossport, ON P0T 2R0

pois.name: Nipigon River Recreation Trail (Paddle-to-the-Sea Park)
pois.note: 10km multi-use trail starting at the marina and running through Eagle Ridge and Lloyd's Lookout to Red Rock — a good legs-stretcher with river views.

pois.name: Ouimet Canyon Provincial Park
pois.note: Boardwalk to two lookout platforms over a sheer 100m-deep, 2km-long gorge — a dramatic short detour about an hour from Thunder Bay.
pois.address: Ouimet Canyon Rd, off Hwy 17, Dorion, ON

pois.name: Top of the Giant Trail
pois.note: The park's marquee hike — a demanding full-day trek to cliff-top views over 200m above Lake Superior from atop the Sleeping Giant formation.
pois.address: Sleeping Giant Provincial Park, Hwy 587, Pass Lake, ON P0T 2M0

pois.name: HWY 17 Hotel
pois.note: 41-room hotel a short walk from the Wawa Goose statue, a reliable overnight base in town.

pois.name: Parkway Motel
pois.note: Award-winning small motel right on the Trans-Canada Highway 4 minutes south of downtown Wawa.

pois.name: Rock Island Lodge

pois.address: 10 Government Dock Rd, Wawa, ON P0S 1K0

pois.name: White River Motel

pois.address: 210 Highway 17 W, White River, ON P0M 3G0

pois.name: Continental Motel & Dining Lounge
pois.note: Second motel option in White River, with an attached dining lounge and jacuzzi rooms.

pois.name: Airport Motor Inn
pois.note: Motor inn right at the main Hwy 17 junction into Marathon.
pois.address: Hwy 17 & Peninsula Rd, Marathon, ON P0T 2E0

pois.name: Drifters Motel & Restaurant
pois.note: Attached motel-and-restaurant combo right on Hwy 17 in Terrace Bay, handy for a one-stop overnight.
pois.address: 3 Simcoe Plaza, Highway 17, Terrace Bay, ON P0T 2W0

pois.name: Nor-West Motel
pois.note: Clean, quiet motel on the highway through Schreiber.

pois.name: Nipigon Travelers Motel

pois.name: Timber Wolf Inn

pois.name: Sawpit Bay Motel & Cabins

pois.address: 13826 Hwy 17 N, Batchawana Bay, ON P0S 1A0

pois.name: Hilltop Motel and Restaurant
pois.note: Renovated motel with kitchenette units about 40 minutes north of Sault Ste. Marie on Hwy 17.
pois.address: 11382 Highway 17 North, Batchawana Bay, ON P0S 1A0

pois.name: Sault Area Hospital
pois.note: Regional hospital and the last major trauma centre before the long remote stretch north to Marathon and Thunder Bay.
pois.address: 750 Great Northern Rd, Sault Ste. Marie, ON P6B 0A8

pois.name: Lady Dunn Health Centre

pois.name: Wawa Pharmacy

pois.name: White River Medical Clinic

pois.name: Wilson Memorial General Hospital

pois.name: Marathon Drug Associates (Guardian IDA)

pois.name: McCausland Hospital

pois.name: Aguasabon Medical Clinic

pois.address: 20B Cartier Drive, Terrace Bay, ON P0T 2W0

pois.name: Nipigon District Memorial Hospital
pois.note: 37-bed hospital with round-the-clock emergency care and labour & delivery, the main medical stop between Terrace Bay and Thunder Bay.

pois.name: Rexall Drug Store (Nipigon)

pois.name: Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre

pois.note: Heavy truck and vehicle repair shop in Wawa's industrial park, useful for major mechanical issues in this remote stretch.

pois.name: Northern Lights Ford

pois.name: D & A Service/Repair & Towing

pois.name: Fountain Tire

pois.name: AUTOPRO Schreiber

zones.label: Boundary Waters, Quetico & Kenora
zones.blurb: Canadian Shield lake country — Quetico's canoe-country quiet gives way to Kenora's Lake of the Woods waterfront.
tips: Quetico is a wilderness park — Dawson Trail is the only real drive-in campground.
Kenora's harbourfront (Husky the Muskie) is an easy stretch-the-legs stop with parking for larger rigs.

safety.cellCoverage: Reliable in Atikokan and Kenora; gaps in Quetico's interior.

pois.name: Johnson's Esso
pois.note: Esso fuel stop in Atikokan on Hwy 11B, handy last fill-up before heading into Quetico.

pois.name: Husky Travel Centre
pois.note: Husky station/truck stop on Hwy 17 E in Kenora with easy big-rig and RV access.
pois.address: 470 Lakeview Drive, Keewatin, Kenora, ON P9N 3P7

pois.name: Red River Co-op Gas Bar
pois.note: Local co-op gas bar along the Hwy 17 corridor through Kenora.

pois.name: Voyageur Bait and Tackle
pois.note: Combined fuel and bait/tackle shop on Hwy 11B in Atikokan, useful trip-planning stop.

pois.name: The Grill at Little Falls

pois.address: 100 Little Falls Road, Atikokan, ON P0T 1C0

pois.name: Sapawe Corner Diner
pois.note: Classic highway diner on Hwy 623, a short detour north of Atikokan off Hwy 11.
pois.address: Highway 11 near Sapawe, Atikokan, ON P0T 1C0

pois.name: Waterside Restaurant (Lakeside Inn)

pois.address: 470 First Avenue S, Kenora, ON P9N 1W5

pois.name: Boathouse Lakeside Grill
pois.note: Waterfront eatery and patio right on the Kenora harbourfront.

pois.name: Dawson Trail Campground (Quetico PP)
pois.note: Quetico's main drive-in campground at French Lake off Hwy 11, sites suit trailers/campervans.
pois.address: 30 Quetico Park Road (45 km east of Atikokan via Hwy 11), Atikokan, ON P0T 1C0
pois.hours: Seasonal: May 15–Oct 13, gate hours vary; winter camping Jan 1–Mar 31

pois.name: Anicinabe Park Campground
pois.note: City-run campground and RV park on Lake of the Woods within Kenora, full hookups available.
pois.address: 955 Golf Course Road, Kenora, ON P9N 0E9

pois.name: Rushing River Provincial Park
pois.note: Popular provincial park east of Kenora on Hwy 17 with RV-friendly sites near a swimming falls.

pois.name: Pye's Landing
pois.note: Lake of the Woods resort/campground in Clearwater Bay, north of Kenora via Hwy 658.

pois.name: Husky the Muskie
pois.note: Giant fibreglass muskie statue at McLeod Park, an iconic Kenora waterfront photo stop.
pois.address: Highway 17 at McLeod Park, Kenora, ON

pois.name: Kenora Harbourfront / McLeod Park
pois.note: Waterfront park and boardwalk on Lake of the Woods, good spot to stretch legs and take photos.
pois.address: Highway 17 at McLeod Park / Harbourfront, Kenora, ON

pois.name: Pickerel Point Trail (Quetico PP)
pois.note: Short, easy interpretive trail near the French Lake park office in Quetico Provincial Park.
pois.address: Quetico Park Road off Hwy 11 (near Dawson Trail Campground), Atikokan, ON P0T 1C0

pois.name: Rushing River Lower Falls Trail
pois.note: Short trail to a scenic waterfall on the Rushing River, just off Hwy 17 east of Kenora.

pois.name: Loon's Nest Plus Inc

pois.address: 704 Mackenzie Avenue East, Atikokan, ON P0T 1C0

pois.name: Esso Gas and Convenient Store
pois.note: 24/7 card-lock pumps with a convenience store right on Hwy 17 through Ignace, roughly the halfway point between Atikokan and Dryden.
pois.hours: Summer: daily 6am–9pm (winter hours shorter) — call ahead

pois.name: Petro-Canada Highway 17 West
pois.note: Petro-Pass truck stop with EV charging on the west edge of Ignace, good for larger rigs.

pois.name: Shell Ignace
pois.note: Second fuel option in town if the Esso or Petro-Canada lines are backed up.

pois.name: Husky (Dryden)
pois.note: 24-hour fuel and convenience stop on Dryden's main commercial strip.

pois.name: Dryden Keystop
pois.note: Truck-stop-style fuel bar on the east side of Dryden, useful for topping up before the long push toward Vermilion Bay.

pois.name: Petro-Canada (Government St, Dryden)
pois.note: Central Dryden fuel stop steps from downtown restaurants and pharmacies.
pois.hours: Daily until approx. 10:00pm — call ahead to confirm

pois.name: Esso Fill N Chill
pois.note: One of the only fuel stops on the long, remote Shabaqua-to-Ignace stretch of Hwy 17 — worth topping up here even if your tank isn't low.

pois.name: Top Valu Shabaqua
pois.note: Gas bar, convenience store and small restaurant right at the Hwy 11/17 split — last easy fuel stop before choosing your route west.

pois.name: Canadian Tire Gas+

pois.name: Husky (Hwy 17 E, Kenora)
pois.note: Eastern-approach fuel stop as you roll into Kenora from Dryden/Vermilion Bay.

pois.name: Shell (2nd St S, Kenora)
pois.note: 24-hour downtown Kenora fuel stop, walkable to waterfront restaurants.

pois.name: Northwoods Motor Inn Restaurant
pois.note: Sit-down breakfast/lunch/dinner dining room attached to Ignace's main motel — a reliable hot meal midway through the corridor.

pois.name: Ignace Tavern & Taxi
pois.note: Local pub-style spot for burgers, wings and pizza a block off Hwy 17 in Ignace.

pois.name: Voyageur Restaurant
pois.note: Family dining attached to the Esso station in the middle of Ignace, easy for a quick group meal.

pois.name: Tower Hill Truck Stop
pois.note: Truck-stop diner with late hours, good backup if other Ignace kitchens are closed.
pois.address: 1030 Main Street (Hwy 17 E), Ignace, ON P0T 1T0

pois.name: B & B Roadhouse Bar and Grill
pois.note: Locally loved for hearty seafood pasta and generous portions — a good sit-down break in Dryden.

pois.name: Patricia Inn Family Restaurant
pois.note: Family-style diner on Dryden's main strip, known for generous portions.

pois.name: Log Cabin Tavern
pois.note: Barbecue tavern just outside downtown Kenora — a casual option away from the tourist strip.
pois.address: 201 Rabbit Lake Road, Kenora, ON P9N 4G8

pois.name: Sunset Inn Kenora & Forest Room Restaurant
pois.note: 24-hour restaurant and lounge on the eastern Hwy 17 strip — useful if you roll into Kenora late.

pois.name: Ristorante Pizzeria Italia

pois.address: 230 First Street South, Kenora, ON P9N 1T3

pois.name: The Hungry Pug
pois.note: Downtown Kenora café/eatery a short walk from the harbourfront.

pois.name: Lake of the Woods Brewing Company

pois.name: Aaron Provincial Park

pois.name: The Willows RV Park & Campground

pois.name: Kenora Bed 'n' Bale RV Park
pois.note: Seasonal RV park close to town with nearby hiking to Rabbit Lake and Garrow Park beach.

pois.name: Greenpines Campground

pois.name: Little Falls Park

pois.address: Little Falls Road, Atikokan, ON P0T 1C0

pois.name: Whiskey Jack Trail (Quetico PP)

zones.label: Manitoba Prairies & Riding Mountain
zones.blurb: Winnipeg's Forks for a city break, then north into Riding Mountain's forested escarpment and its free-roaming bison herd.
tips: The Forks Market is the easiest one-stop lunch for a big group.
Lake Audy's bison enclosure is a drive-through — best light early morning or late afternoon.
Wasagaming Campground has full hookups; book ahead for September weekends.

safety.cellCoverage: Good in Winnipeg and Wasagaming townsite; spottier in the park's backcountry (Grey Owl's Cabin trail).
safety.nearestHospital: Winnipeg or McCreary/Onanole near the park
safety.note: Standard 911 coverage on Hwy 1 and Hwy 10.

pois.name: Petro-Pass Truck Stop (Petro-Canada)
pois.note: Big rig-friendly truck stop at Hwy 1 & Hwy 16 junction, Portage la Prairie.
pois.address: 2199 Saskatchewan Ave W, Portage la Prairie, MB R1N 3B2

pois.name: Petro-Canada - 1284 Portage Avenue
pois.note: Convenient fuel stop on Portage Ave heading west out of downtown Winnipeg.

pois.name: Co-op Gas Bar - 3755 Portage Avenue

pois.name: Petro-Canada - Minnedosa (Hwy 1 & Hwy 10)

zones.label: Calgary & Canadian Rockies Front Range
zones.blurb: The postcard stretch — Banff, Lake Louise, Moraine Lake, and Yoho's waterfalls, all within a couple hours of Calgary.
tips: Moraine Lake and Lake Louise often require a shuttle/reservation in peak season — check Parks Canada ahead.
Banff/Yoho campgrounds book out fast; reserve well ahead for Sept weekends.
This is the most tourist-dense zone on the route — arrive at trailheads early.

safety.cellCoverage: Good in Banff/Canmore townsites; drops off along the Icefields Parkway and in Yoho's backcountry.
safety.nearestHospital: Banff Mineral Springs Hospital or Canmore General
safety.note: Wildlife country — bear spray recommended on any trail here.

zones.label: Channeled Scablands & Inland Northwest
zones.blurb: A dramatic border-to-lake crossing through Ice Age flood scars at Dry Falls and Grand Coulee, then down into the pine-covered lake country of Spokane and Coeur d'Alene.
tips: Fuel up before Coulee City or Grand Coulee — stations thin out fast on the scablands stretch between Omak and Davenport.
The Dry Falls Visitor Center itself is closed for renovation through the end of 2026; a mobile info stand runs in the day-use lot at Sun Lakes–Dry Falls State Park instead, 3 miles south on Hwy 17.
Grand Coulee Dam tours and the laser light show only run seasonally (tours resume late May); check hours before planning your stop there in October.

safety.cellCoverage: Decent along US-97 through Tonasket/Omak and on US-2/WA-155 near Coulee City and Grand Coulee, but expect dead zones in the scablands between Coulee City and Grand Coulee Dam and on back roads around Steamboat Rock. Strong coverage resumes on US-2 into Davenport and I-90 to Spokane and Coeur d'Alene.
safety.nearestHospital: Mid-Valley Hospital (Omak), Lincoln Hospital (Davenport), Providence Sacred Heart Medical Center (Spokane, Level II trauma), or Kootenai Health (Coeur d'Alene)
safety.note: October daytime highs in the scablands are mild but nights can dip near freezing; watch for early-season black ice on shaded stretches of WA-155 and US-2 near the coulees, and for deer/elk crossing at dawn and dusk on the two-lane roads around Banks Lake and Lake Coeur d'Alene.

zones.label: Bitterroot Valley & Big Sky Country
zones.blurb: From the Idaho line at Lookout Pass through Missoula's river-town energy and Butte's copper-mining scars, down the gold-rush ghost streets of Virginia City and the trout water of the Madison Valley, right up to Yellowstone's west gate.
tips: Fuel and services are plentiful in Missoula and Butte but thin out fast on US-287/US-191 south of Twin Bridges — top off before Ennis or West Yellowstone.
Red Mountain and other BLM campgrounds on the lower Madison River are first-come, first-served in fall — aim to arrive with daylight left to find a site.
West Yellowstone is your last real grocery/gear stop before the park gate; cell coverage and dining choices drop off sharply once you're inside Yellowstone.

safety.cellCoverage: Strong through Missoula and Butte; patchy to absent through the Madison Valley (Twin Bridges–Ennis) and largely absent once inside Yellowstone.
safety.nearestHospital: Missoula (Providence St. Patrick or Community Medical Center), Butte (St. James Healthcare), or the 24-hour ER at Madison Valley Medical Center in Ennis
safety.note: Fall nights regularly drop below freezing in the Madison Valley and at West Yellowstone's ~6,600 ft elevation; watch for early snow on US-191 near West Yellowstone and Targhee Pass in October.

zones.label: Yellowstone — Geyser Country
zones.blurb: Two full days based at Madison Campground, right where the Firehole and Gibbon rivers meet — geothermal basins, the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, and Hayden Valley wildlife are all within easy reach, but by Oct 9–10 most in-park lodges and several campgrounds have already closed for the season.
tips: Fuel up before entering the park — there is NO gas at Madison Junction itself; the nearest in-park stations are Old Faithful, Fishing Bridge, or back in West Yellowstone, so top off at the gateway town first.

Madison Campground and Old Faithful Inn both close mid-October (Madison ~Oct 18, Old Faithful Inn Oct 12 in 2026) — you're right at the edge of the season, so confirm current status at the entrance station or nps.gov/yell before counting on any specific facility.

Fairy Falls Trailhead parking fills fast even in shoulder season; the Grand Prismatic Overlook Trail from the same lot is the best non-boardwalk view of the spring — have the Midway Geyser Basin lot as backup a mile north.

safety.cellCoverage: Little to no cell service anywhere in the park interior, including Madison, the geyser basins, and Hayden Valley — download offline maps and tell someone your plan before heading out.
safety.nearestHospital: Old Faithful Clinic (in-season) or Billings Clinic West Yellowstone for the geyser-basin area; Mammoth Clinic is open year-round but is over an hour from Madison.
safety.note: This is bear and bison country — bear spray recommended on any trail, and never approach wildlife (bison gore more visitors than any other animal in the park). Boardwalks near thermal features are mandatory — ground can be a thin crust over near-boiling water.

pois.name: Conoco (Firehole Avenue)
pois.note: Central West Yellowstone gas stop, easy last-fuel top-off before entering the West Entrance — there is no fuel at Madison Junction inside the park.

pois.name: Canyon St. Exxon
pois.note: 24-hour station on Canyon Street in West Yellowstone, a reliable option any time of day before or after the park.
pois.address: 215 N Canyon St, West Yellowstone, MT 59758

pois.name: Eagle Chevron
pois.note: Another central West Yellowstone fuel option a short walk from downtown restaurants.

pois.name: Old Faithful Service Station
pois.note: In-park 24-hour credit-card fueling near the Old Faithful General Store — the closest in-park gas to Madison Campground, about 16 miles south.

pois.name: Fishing Bridge Service Station
pois.note: In-park station near Fishing Bridge with unleaded, diesel and propane, plus RV/auto repair and towing — but note its 2026 season ends around Oct 1, so it may already be closed by Oct 9–10.
pois.hours: Seasonal: ~May 19–Oct 1, 2026 — may be closed by your visit dates, verify at an entrance station

pois.name: Old Faithful Inn Dining Room
pois.note: Sit-down dining inside the historic 1904 log-timber Old Faithful Inn — reservations recommended; the Inn itself closes for the season Oct 12, 2026, so it should still be open for an Oct 9–10 visit but call ahead to confirm.
pois.hours: Seasonal through Oct 12, 2026 — call ahead to confirm dinner reservations

pois.name: Old Faithful Snow Lodge Geyser Grill
pois.note: Casual quick-service option next to Old Faithful, useful backup if the Inn's dining room is fully booked; runs later into October than most other in-park food service.

pois.name: Obsidian Dining Room, Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel
pois.note: Open year-round sit-down option at Mammoth if a day trip extends north — about 1.5 hours from Madison, worth knowing since Mammoth stays open through winter.

pois.name: Slippery Otter Pub
pois.note: Popular West Yellowstone gastropub with elk and bison burgers, wide beer selection — a solid dinner option the nights you're staged at the gateway town.
pois.address: 139 N Canyon St, West Yellowstone, MT 59758

pois.name: Beartooth Barbecue
pois.note: West Yellowstone's original Southern barbecue joint since 1999, with a strong local-brewery beer list.

pois.name: Madison Campground General Store
pois.note: Small mercantile at Madison Campground itself for snacks, sundries and camp basics — not a full grocery, plan main meals elsewhere.

pois.name: Old Faithful General Store
pois.note: Grab-and-go food service and grocery basics near Old Faithful, open daily through Oct 18, 2026.

pois.name: Madison Campground
pois.note: Base camp for these two days, right at the confluence of the Firehole and Gibbon rivers where they form the Madison River. Reservable through Yellowstone National Park Lodges for 2026 (Recreation.gov takes over starting 2027); flush toilets, dump station, no showers on-site. 2026 season runs roughly May 1–Oct 18, so it should be open for Oct 9–10 but confirm — dates can shift with weather.
pois.address: 30 Madison Campground Rd, Yellowstone National Park, WY 82190
pois.hours: Seasonal: ~May 1–Oct 18, 2026; check-in office 8am–5pm; generators permitted 8am–8pm at RV/combo sites only

pois.name: Canyon Campground
pois.note: Large campground near the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone rim — good if Madison is full, but its 2026 season is shorter, closing around Sept 20, so it will likely already be closed for an Oct 9–10 trip.
pois.hours: Seasonal: ~May 29–Sept 20, 2026 — likely closed by early October, verify before relying on it

pois.name: Norris Campground
pois.note: Historically a first-come-first-served campground near Norris Geyser Basin, but it has been closed for the 2026 season (and several prior years) due to staffing limits — do not plan around it.

pois.name: Grand Prismatic Spring / Midway Geyser Basin
pois.note: Yellowstone's largest hot spring and the park's most photographed feature — vivid rainbow colors come from heat-loving microbial mats ringing the pool. Boardwalk loop is short and wheelchair accessible; go early or late to beat crowds and steam glare.

pois.name: Grand Prismatic Overlook Trail
pois.note: 0.5-mile, ~105 ft climb from the Fairy Falls Trailhead lot to an elevated overlook — the only vantage point that shows Grand Prismatic's full rainbow shape from above. Trailhead lot is small and fills early; Midway Geyser Basin lot a mile north is the fallback.

pois.name: Fairy Falls Trail
pois.note: Easy-to-moderate ~5-mile round trip (from Fairy Falls Trailhead) past the Grand Prismatic overlook spur to a graceful 200-foot waterfall — can continue on to Imperial Geyser for a longer loop.

pois.name: Firehole Canyon Drive & Firehole Falls
pois.note: Scenic 2-mile one-way side road just south of Madison Junction past 800-ft lava canyon walls, a 40-ft waterfall, and one of only two swimming holes in the park (roadside parking only, no formal lot, closed in high spring water). A quick, easy add-on right next to camp.

pois.name: Norris Geyser Basin
pois.note: Yellowstone's hottest, oldest and most volatile thermal area — home to Steamboat Geyser, the world's tallest active geyser (300–400 ft eruptions, unpredictable, ranging days to decades apart). Porcelain Basin and Back Basin loops together take 2–3 hours; boardwalks only, ground can give way to scalding water.

pois.name: Artist Paint Pots
pois.note: Easy 1-mile boardwalk/trail about 5 miles south of Norris through bubbling mud pots, small geysers and steam vents — a good lower-crowd stop, 30–60 minutes.

pois.name: Old Faithful & Upper Geyser Basin
pois.note: The park's most famous geyser, erupting roughly every 60–110 minutes (average interval creeping longer over recent decades); the surrounding Upper Geyser Basin boardwalk has the highest concentration of geysers on Earth. About 16 miles south of Madison — plan a half-day.

pois.name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone / Artist Point
pois.note: Vivid yellow-and-orange canyon walls (the source of the park's name) framing the 308-ft Lower Falls — Artist Point is the classic overlook, about 1.25 hours from Madison.

pois.name: Hayden Valley
pois.note: Wide-open glacial valley along the Grand Loop between Canyon and Fishing Bridge — one of the best wildlife-viewing stretches in the park for bison herds, elk, and occasionally wolves or grizzlies; go early morning or dusk.

pois.name: Old Faithful Inn
pois.note: Iconic 1904 log lodge, the largest log structure in the world — closes for the 2026 season Oct 12, so it will just barely still be open for Oct 9–10, but book far ahead and confirm status.

pois.name: Old Faithful Snow Lodge & Cabins
pois.note: More modern option near Old Faithful with cabins and hotel rooms; 2026 summer/fall season runs to about Oct 11, so also right at the edge of closing for your dates.

pois.name: Stage Coach Inn
pois.note: Landmark 83-room hotel at the West Entrance gateway with indoor pool and sauna — a comfortable option if not camping every night.

pois.name: Alpine Motel
pois.note: Small family-run motel two blocks from the West Entrance, simple and central.

pois.name: Explorer Cabins at Yellowstone
pois.note: Private cabins with kitchenettes on the edge of West Yellowstone, good if you want more space than a motel room without a full RV setup.

pois.name: Old Faithful Medical Clinic
pois.note: In-park clinic near Old Faithful for injuries and illness, typically open late April through late October — should be operating for an Oct 9–10 visit but call ahead this late in the season.

pois.name: Mammoth Clinic
pois.note: Open year-round, the most reliable in-park medical option once shoulder-season clinics elsewhere start winding down — about 1.5 hours from Madison.

pois.name: Billings Clinic West Yellowstone
pois.note: Primary and urgent care clinic in the gateway town, took over from the former Community Health Partners clinic in 2023 — the closest full urgent care to Madison Campground outside the park.

pois.name: Jake's Automotive & Tire
pois.note: Full-service repair shop with tires and 24-hour towing/recovery in West Yellowstone — there is essentially no auto repair inside the park itself, so this is the closest real option.

pois.name: Fishing Bridge RV/Auto Repair
pois.note: Limited in-park RV and automotive repair with towing tied to the Fishing Bridge service station — seasonal only and likely closed by early October (station season ends ~Oct 1), so treat West Yellowstone as the reliable fallback.
pois.hours: Seasonal, roughly May 19–Oct 1 — likely closed by your visit dates

zones.label: Lamar Valley & Absaroka Front
zones.blurb: Yellowstone's wildest corner — Norris to Canyon to Tower-Roosevelt, then the open grass of Lamar Valley (bison, wolves, grizzlies) before a weather-decision climb over Dunraven Pass or a scenic bailout via Cooke City and the Chief Joseph Scenic Byway down to Cody.
tips: Dunraven Pass (8,859 ft) can see snow even in early-to-mid October — check current NPS road status before committing; the alternate is Lamar Valley to Cooke City then Chief Joseph Scenic Byway (Hwy 296) over Dead Indian Pass into Cody.

Fuel up (and check tires/fluids) before leaving Yellowstone's interior or in Cooke City — there is no gas, repair, or tow service between Cooke City/Silver Gate and Cody, roughly 75 miles via the Chief Joseph Byway/North Fork route.
Lamar Valley is Yellowstone's best wildlife-watching stretch — pull all the way off the road at marked pullouts, bring binoculars/a scope, and go slow at dawn/dusk for bison, elk, and wolves.

safety.cellCoverage: No reliable cell service through most of Yellowstone's interior, Lamar Valley, or Cooke City/Silver Gate; some signal returns in Cody. Sunlight Basin and Dead Indian Pass are also dead zones.
safety.nearestHospital: West Park Hospital (Cody Regional Health), 707 Sheridan Ave, Cody, WY — 24-hour ER; nothing comparable exists between Tower-Roosevelt and Cody.
safety.note: Grizzly and wolf country — carry bear spray, never approach wildlife (100 yards from bears/wolves, 25 yards from bison/elk), and treat Cooke City/Silver Gate as having minimal services outside summer season.

pois.name: Cooke City Sinclair (Cooke City Exxon/Sinclair)
pois.note: Small-town Sinclair fuel stop on Main Street, also sells pizza, doughnuts, and breakfast sandwiches — last realistic fuel before the long haul to Cody.
pois.address: 115 Main St E, Cooke City, MT 59020

pois.name: Sinclair - Cody (1502 Sheridan Ave)
pois.note: In-town Sinclair with pay-at-pump, RV-height canopy, and propane refills — a reliable Cody fill-up.

pois.name: Sinclair - Cody (124 Yellowstone Ave, fuel only)
pois.note: Fuel-only Sinclair station near downtown Cody, a quick top-off before heading toward Yellowstone's East or Northeast Entrance.

pois.name: Canyon Village Gas Station
pois.note: NPS-concession fuel at Canyon Village, the last easy fill-up before heading toward Tower-Roosevelt and Lamar Valley.

pois.name: Tower-Roosevelt Gas Station
pois.note: Small seasonal fuel stop at the Tower-Roosevelt junction, the last gas before entering Lamar Valley eastbound.

pois.name: Cooke City General Store
pois.note: National Register-listed general store operating since 1886, with original fixtures and a deli counter — groceries, snacks, and fishing licenses.

pois.name: Beartooth Cafe
pois.note: Long-running Cooke City roadhouse on the Beartooth Highway known for burgers, ribs, and a big beer selection.

pois.name: Millstone Pizza Company & Brewery
pois.note: Pizza, brewery, and arcade/sports-bar spot on Sheridan Ave — a solid family-friendly dinner stop in Cody.

pois.name: Cassie's Steakhouse & Saloon
pois.note: Historic Cody steakhouse and saloon with live music and dancing — kitchen opens at 4pm, closed Sun/Mon.

pois.name: Buffalo Bill's Irma Hotel Restaurant & Saloon
pois.note: Historic hotel restaurant built by Buffalo Bill Cody in 1902, famous for its cherrywood back bar gifted by Queen Victoria — classic Western dining.

pois.name: Wyoming's Rib & Chop House
pois.note: Regional steakhouse chain outpost on Sheridan Ave serving steaks, ribs, and seafood — popular sit-down dinner option in Cody.

pois.name: Hogan and Luce Campground (BLM)
pois.note: Small BLM campground with 5 individual sites plus a group site beside Hogan Reservoir, rebuilt to ADA standards in 2017–18; bear-proof boxes, boat ramp, fishing. Reached via Hwy 120 north then Park County Rd 7RP — tonight's overnight.

pois.name: Newton Creek Campground
pois.note: 31-site Shoshone National Forest campground on the North Fork/Buffalo Bill Cody Scenic Byway, 37 miles west of Cody and 16 miles from Yellowstone's East Entrance; hard-sided camping only, frequent grizzly activity, no reservations.

pois.name: Slough Creek Campground
pois.note: Small, primitive NPS campground on a 2-mile gravel spur off the Lamar Valley road, prime early-morning wolf-watching base.

pois.name: Pebble Creek Campground
pois.note: Small NPS campground in a quiet meadow near the Yellowstone Northeast Entrance, a good jumping-off point for Lamar Valley and Cooke City.

pois.name: Tower Fall Campground
pois.note: NPS campground right at the Tower Fall trailhead, on the north side of the climb up Dunraven Pass.

pois.name: Soda Butte Lodge
pois.note: The only full-service hotel in Cooke City — 32 rooms, Prospector Restaurant, saloon; 4 minutes from Yellowstone's Northeast Entrance.

pois.name: Antlers Lodge
pois.note: Historic 1913 log-cabin lodge (originally the Shaw Lodge, Cooke City's first tourist facility) with individual cabins near the Beartooth Mountains.

pois.name: Buffalo Bill's Irma Hotel
pois.note: Historic 1902 hotel built by Buffalo Bill Cody himself and named for his daughter Irma; still operating as a hotel today in downtown Cody.

pois.name: Holiday Inn Cody at Buffalo Bill Village Resort
pois.note: Largest of the three Buffalo Bill Village properties, full-service with pool, restaurant, and airport shuttle, 8 blocks from the Buffalo Bill Center of the West.

pois.name: Comfort Inn at Buffalo Bill Village Resort
pois.note: Budget-friendlier sister property at Buffalo Bill Village, free breakfast and WiFi.

pois.name: Lamar Valley (Lamar River / Confluence Overlook)
pois.note: Open glacial valley nicknamed 'America's Serengeti' — the best single stretch in Yellowstone for bison herds, elk, and wolf-watching; pull all the way off at marked pullouts.

pois.name: Slough Creek / Hitching Post Pullout
pois.note: One of the most reliable wolf-watching spots in the park — the Junction Butte pack has denned in this area for years; spotting scopes line up here at dawn.

pois.name: Soda Butte Creek
pois.note: Wide meadow along the road between Lamar Valley and the Northeast Entrance, good for grizzlies and pronghorn.

pois.name: Tower Fall
pois.note: 132-foot waterfall dropping through volcanic-breccia pinnacles, easy overlook a short walk from the parking area.

pois.name: Dunraven Pass
pois.note: 8,859-ft high point on the Grand Loop Road between Tower and Canyon — the weather-decision point for this route; can close or ice over even in early-to-mid October.
pois.nearTown: Between Tower-Roosevelt and Canyon Village, Yellowstone NP

pois.name: Dead Indian Pass Overlook
pois.note: 8,071-ft summit on the Chief Joseph Scenic Byway (Hwy 296) with a turnout, interpretive signs, and restrooms; sweeping views over Sunlight Basin and the Clarks Fork of the Yellowstone.

pois.name: Sunlight Basin / Chief Joseph Scenic Byway
pois.note: 46-mile byway (WY-296) from Cody toward Cooke City, descending seven switchbacks off Dead Indian Pass into a broad basin along Sunlight Creek — a scenic weather-alternate route between Lamar Valley and Cody.

pois.name: Buffalo Bill Dam & Visitor Center
pois.note: 1910-built dam (one of the tallest in the world at the time) spanning the Shoshone River Canyon, with a visitor center on the reservoir; open daily May–Sept.
pois.hours: May & Sep: Mon–Fri 8am–6pm, Sat–Sun 9am–5pm; Jun–Aug: Mon–Fri 8am–7pm, Sat–Sun 9am–5pm

pois.name: West Park Hospital (Cody Regional Health)
pois.note: Cody's main hospital with a 24-hour emergency department — the nearest real hospital for the entire Lamar Valley/Cooke City/Sunlight Basin stretch of this route.

pois.name: Walmart Pharmacy Cody
pois.note: In-store pharmacy on Yellowstone Ave, a convenient prescription/OTC stop while passing through Cody.

pois.name: Albertsons Pharmacy Cody
pois.note: Grocery-store pharmacy on 17th St for prescriptions, flu shots, and basic medical supplies.

pois.name: Mammoth Clinic (Yellowstone National Park)
pois.note: The park's main year-round clinic, roughly 90 minutes from Lamar Valley via Tower-Roosevelt — handles urgent care inside Yellowstone; for anything serious, continue to West Park Hospital in Cody instead.

pois.name: Les Schwab Tire Center Cody
pois.note: Full tire, alignment, and brake shop just west of the Cody Walmart — the last major repair option before heading back into Yellowstone or over Sunlight Basin.

zones.label: Bighorn Mountains & Devils Tower
zones.blurb: A big day of driving — out of the Cody/Powell irrigation flats, up and over the Bighorns on the Shell Canyon switchbacks, down into Sheridan's ranch-country downtown, then east across the plains to camp in the shadow of Devils Tower.
tips: Fill up in Sheridan or Moorcroft before continuing east — fuel options thin out fast between Burgess Junction and Devils Tower.
Shell Canyon's grade (US-14 between Shell and Burgess Junction) is steep and switchbacked — check brakes and go slow in a loaded Sprinter, especially eastbound descents.
Belle Fourche River Campground at the monument is first-come, first-served with no hookups — arrive by early-mid afternoon in shoulder season to be sure of a pull-through site.

safety.cellCoverage: Decent in Powell, Lovell, and Sheridan; drops to little or no signal through Shell Canyon and over Burgess Junction/the Bighorn summit; patchy again around Devils Tower and Hulett.
safety.nearestHospital: Sheridan Memorial Hospital (1401 W 5th St, Sheridan) for the western half of the day; Powell Valley Healthcare (777 Ave H, Powell) covers the Cody/Powell start.
safety.note: US-14 over the Bighorns gains roughly 5,000 ft with sustained grades and hairpins — watch for logging trucks, wildlife, and sudden mountain weather even in October; the highway can close for snow.

pois.name: Maverik Adventure's First Stop (Powell)
pois.note: 24-hour fuel and convenience stop with diesel pumps on the east side of Powell, a good first fill of the day.

pois.name: Big Horn Co-Op Marketing Association (Powell)
