pois.name: Maverik Adventure's First Stop (Lovell)
pois.note: Fuel and snacks on Main Street in Lovell, the last sizeable town before climbing toward the Bighorns via Shell.

pois.name: Sinclair Gas Station Lovell
pois.note: Sinclair-brand convenience store and pumps on E Main St in Lovell.

pois.name: Les Schwab Tire Center (Sheridan) – also fuel-adjacent stop
pois.note: Not a fuel stop itself, but Coffeen Ave through Sheridan has several stations clustered nearby — good spot to fill up before the run east to Devils Tower.

pois.name: Coffee Cup Fuel Stop (Moorcroft)
pois.note: Well-known truck-stop-style fuel and food stop on I-90 in Moorcroft, the last major fuel before the Devils Tower turnoff on US-14.

pois.name: KUM & GO / Maverik (Moorcroft, US-14/16)
pois.note: Fuel stop at the junction area where US-14 splits north toward Devils Tower and Hulett.

pois.name: Sinclair / Rolling Metal Sinclair (Hulett)
pois.note: Small-town gas stop in Hulett, useful last-chance fuel a short drive from Devils Tower's north/west approach.

pois.name: Devils Tower Trading Post / General Store gas
pois.note: Small store with fuel pumps right outside the Devils Tower National Monument entrance on WY-110.

pois.name: Big Horn Co-Op Marketing (Cody area)
pois.note: Co-op fuel option on the western end of this leg, useful if topping off before leaving the Cody area.

pois.name: Frackelton's
pois.note: New American dinner spot in a historic downtown Sheridan building, known for steaks and original cocktails.

pois.name: Cowboy Cafe
pois.note: Hearty diner-style breakfasts and lunches in downtown Sheridan, a local favorite for a road-trip refuel.

pois.name: The Warehouse Gastropub
pois.note: Casual gastropub in downtown Sheridan with a wide beer list and elevated pub food.

pois.name: Pony Grill and Bar
pois.note: Longtime downtown Sheridan bar and grill, reasonably priced and friendly for a mid-drive lunch.

pois.name: Java Moon
pois.note: Specialty coffee shop in downtown Sheridan, a good caffeine stop before or after the Bighorn crossing.

pois.name: Nonna's Italian Kitchen
pois.note: Family-style Italian restaurant in downtown Sheridan.

pois.name: Campstool Cafe (Devils Tower KOA)
pois.note: On-site cafe and saloon at the Devils Tower/Black Hills KOA, serving buffalo burgers, salads, and steaks with tower views.

pois.name: Devils Tower View Campground & Cafe
pois.note: Casual cafe attached to a private campground just outside the monument, with a direct view of the tower from the patio.

pois.name: 77 Steakhouse and Saloon
pois.note: Small-town steakhouse and bar in Hulett, a solid dinner option if overnighting near the monument's west side.

pois.name: Ponderosa Cafe & Bar
pois.note: Classic small-town Wyoming cafe and bar in Hulett serving diner staples.

pois.name: Remy's Diner
pois.note: Roadside diner in Moorcroft on the way to or from Devils Tower, good for a quick sit-down meal.

pois.name: Belle Fourche River Campground (Devils Tower NM)
pois.note: First-come, first-served NPS campground right at the base of the tower along the Belle Fourche River; two loops, 45 sites (43 pull-through for RVs up to 35 ft), no hookups, flush toilets and potable water. $20/night, 14-day limit. This is the planned overnight stop for the night of Oct 12.

pois.name: Devils Tower / Black Hills KOA Journey
pois.note: Private campground just outside the monument gate with full hookups, showers, a general store, and the Campstool Cafe — a backup if the NPS campground is full.
pois.hours: Seasonal, roughly Apr–Oct — call ahead for late-season dates

pois.name: Devils Tower View Campground
pois.note: Small private campground with direct tower views and an on-site cafe, another backup option near the monument.

pois.name: Sibley Lake Campground
pois.note: USFS campground on a scenic alpine lake right on the Bighorn Scenic Byway near Burgess Junction, elevation ~7,900 ft; some sites have electric hookups. Open roughly June–mid-September.

pois.name: Prune Creek Campground
pois.note: USFS campground on the South Fork Tongue River near Burgess Junction, 20 nonelectric sites with vault toilets and hand-pump water — quiet lodgepole-pine setting for a Bighorns overnight.

pois.name: Owen Creek Campground
pois.note: USFS campground along the North Tongue River corridor in the Bighorns near Burgess Junction, a quieter alternative to Sibley Lake.

pois.name: North Tongue Campground
pois.note: USFS campground on US-14A near Burgess Junction, in the same high-country cluster as Sibley Lake and Prune Creek.

pois.name: Shell Falls Interpretive Site
pois.note: Short boardwalk loop overlooking a 120-ft waterfall plunging through granite Shell Canyon; interpretive signage on the canyon's fossil-bearing walls. Open Memorial Day through mid-September, 9:30am–5pm.

pois.name: Shell Canyon (Bighorn Scenic Byway, US-14)
pois.note: Dramatic switchback descent/climb through a deep limestone-and-granite canyon named for embedded shell fossils; the most scenic driving stretch of the day.

pois.name: Burgess Junction Overlooks (US-14)
pois.note: High alpine summit area (~8,000+ ft) where US-14 and US-14A meet, with sweeping views over the Bighorn high country and access to Sibley Lake and Sheep Mountain viewpoints.

pois.name: Medicine Wheel / Medicine Mountain National Historic Landmark
pois.note: Sacred Native American stone medicine wheel (82 ft diameter, 28 spokes) atop Medicine Mountain, used for over 7,000 years by Plains tribes for ceremony and celestial observation; reached via a short detour on US-14A and a ~1.5-mile walk from the parking area.

pois.name: Devils Tower National Monument
pois.note: America's first national monument (1906) — a 1,267-ft igneous rock tower rising above the plains, with the 1.3-mile paved Tower Trail circling its base. The centerpiece of the day.
pois.hours: Park grounds open 24 hours; Visitor Center hours seasonal

pois.name: Devils Tower Visitor Center
pois.note: NPS visitor center at the base of the tower with exhibits on the monument's geology, climbing history, and Native American cultural significance.

pois.name: Joyner Ridge Trail
pois.note: Quieter 1.5-mile loop trail on the north side of the monument with some of the best distant tower views and fewer crowds than the main Tower Trail.

pois.name: Sheridan Inn
pois.note: Historic 1893 hotel in downtown Sheridan once co-owned by Buffalo Bill Cody, now a boutique inn and restaurant.

pois.name: Mill Inn
pois.note: Historic 42-room hotel in a converted flour mill on Coffeen Ave, known for its breakfast and Western character.

pois.name: Best Western Sheridan Center
pois.note: Full-service hotel with indoor pool and dining room on North Main St in Sheridan.

pois.name: Holiday Inn Sheridan Convention Center
pois.note: Large convention hotel near I-90 in Sheridan with well-appointed rooms.

pois.name: Best Western Devils Tower Inn
pois.note: Standard hotel in Hulett, the closest sizeable town to Devils Tower with reliable lodging.

pois.name: The Lodge at Devils Tower
pois.note: Secluded B&B-style lodge roughly 7-11 miles from the monument with mountain views, an alternative to camping.

pois.name: The Hulett Motel
pois.note: Simple, budget-friendly motel in the small town of Hulett, minutes from Devils Tower.

pois.name: Devils Tower Lodge
pois.note: B&B close to the monument entrance, popular with climbers and photographers wanting an early start.

pois.name: Powell Valley Healthcare
pois.note: Regional hospital with a 24-hour emergency department, the main medical facility at the start of this leg.

pois.name: Sheridan Memorial Hospital
pois.note: Full-service hospital with 24-hour ER, the key medical stop between the Bighorns crossing and Devils Tower.

pois.name: Sheridan Memorial Hospital Urgent Care
pois.note: Walk-in urgent care clinic in Sheridan for non-emergency issues, faster than the ER for minor injuries or illness.

pois.name: North Big Horn Hospital
pois.note: Small critical-access hospital in Lovell with an emergency department, useful if issues arise before the Bighorn climb.

pois.name: Campbell County Memorial Hospital
pois.note: Nearest larger hospital to the Devils Tower/Moorcroft area, about an hour south in Gillette — fallback if Sundance or Hulett clinics can't handle an issue.

pois.name: Crook County Medical Services District
pois.note: Small critical-access hospital in Sundance, the closest hospital-level care to Devils Tower and Hulett.

pois.name: Rimrock Tire
pois.note: Tire and general auto repair shop in Powell covering everything from oil changes to engine work.

pois.name: Interstate Tire Service
pois.note: Tire repair, alignment, and roadside assistance shop in Powell.

pois.name: Les Schwab Tire Center (Sheridan)
pois.note: Full-service tire shop on Coffeen Ave in Sheridan handling tires, brakes, batteries, and alignments — a solid mid-route check before or after the Bighorn crossing.

pois.name: Gills Point S Tire & Auto Service (Sheridan)
pois.note: General tire and mechanical repair shop in Sheridan.

pois.name: Firestone Complete Auto Care (Sheridan)
pois.note: Chain auto repair shop in Sheridan for tires, brakes, and general mechanical work.

pois.name: Ridgeline Auto Repair
pois.note: Family-owned auto repair shop serving Powell, Cody, and Lovell.

pois.name: Bear Co. Tire
pois.note: Tire shop and auto repair serving Cody, Powell, and Wapiti — useful before starting the day's drive.

zones.label: Black Hills Gateway & Badlands
zones.blurb: From Devils Tower's igneous spire through Spearfish Canyon's waterfalls and Deadwood's Wild West streets, then east across I-90 into the eroded spires of the Badlands and on to Sioux Falls.
tips: Fill up in Spearfish, Wall, Kadoka, or Chamberlain — fuel stops thin out fast once you're on Badlands Loop Road or Sage Creek Rim Road.
Sage Creek Campground is free and first-come, first-served with zero hookups or water — bring everything you need and expect bison wandering through camp.
Notch Trail involves a log ladder and an exposed ledge; skip it if rain has made the clay slick, since Badlands clay becomes nearly impassable when wet.

safety.cellCoverage: Solid in Spearfish, Deadwood, Wall, Chamberlain, and Sioux Falls; unreliable to nonexistent inside Badlands National Park, especially on Sage Creek Rim Road.
safety.nearestHospital: Monument Health Spearfish (Spearfish) or Monument Health Rapid City for the Black Hills/Wall/Badlands stretch; Sanford USD Medical Center or Avera McKennan in Sioux Falls for the eastern end.
safety.note: Badlands National Park has no hospital or gas inside park boundaries — the nearest full-service ER from Cedar Pass is roughly an hour away in Rapid City. Standard 911 coverage applies where cell signal exists.

pois.name: Tower Valley Ag Supply (Sinclair)
pois.note: The main fuel stop in tiny Hulett, WY, just off the route from Devils Tower; also sells basic supplies.

pois.name: Main Street Conoco
pois.note: Convenient in-town fuel stop on Spearfish's Main Street corridor.

pois.name: Sinclair (Deadwood)
pois.note: Fuel stop right on Main Street in downtown Deadwood, handy before or after the historic district.

pois.name: Corner Pantry
pois.note: Convenience store and fuel stop just off I-90 Exit 110, the last easy gas before entering Badlands National Park from the west.

pois.name: Common Cents Food Stores
pois.note: Fuel and snacks a block off I-90 Exit 110 in Wall, a reliable top-off point before the Badlands Loop Road.

pois.name: Kadoka Gas & Go
pois.note: Conoco/Phillips 66 fuel stop on Kadoka's main highway strip, a good top-off between Badlands and Chamberlain.

pois.name: Sinclair Truckstop (Kadoka)
pois.note: Truck-stop fuel and diesel on the same strip as Kadoka Gas & Go, easy big-rig access.

pois.name: Badlands Travel Stop
pois.note: Fuel and convenience stop with a large lot and clean restrooms, just south of Kadoka.

pois.name: C&E Enterprises Cenex
pois.note: 24-hour Cenex station in Chamberlain with an attached Dairy Queen, a good fuel-and-food combo stop.

pois.name: Flying J Travel Center
pois.note: Large 24-hour travel center on I-90/I-29 with diesel, showers, and RV-friendly pumps for the Sioux Falls approach.
pois.address: 5201 N Granite Ln, Sioux Falls, SD 57104

pois.name: Love's Travel Stop
pois.note: 24-hour truck stop at I-90 Exit 399, a reliable fuel-up on the way into or out of Sioux Falls.
pois.address: 5301 N Cliff Ave, Sioux Falls, SD 57104

pois.name: Cheyenne Crossing Store & Cafe
pois.note: Historic trading-post store and cafe famous for Indian tacos, at the south end of Spearfish Canyon where US-14A meets US-85.

pois.name: Spearfish Canyon Lodge & Latchstring Restaurant
pois.note: Historic 1906-era lodge restaurant in the heart of Spearfish Canyon serving breakfast through dinner; also functions as area lodging.

pois.name: Saloon No. 10 / Deadwood Social Club
pois.note: Iconic 1876 saloon and museum where Wild Bill Hickok was shot, with the Deadwood Social Club steakhouse upstairs for a real sit-down meal.

pois.name: Wall Drug Store Cafe
pois.note: Legendary roadside cafe inside the sprawling Wall Drug complex, famous for homemade donuts and free ice water since 1936.

pois.name: Cedar Pass Lodge Restaurant
pois.note: The only sit-down dining inside Badlands National Park, serving breakfast through dinner including Sioux/fry-bread specialties; open seasonally April-October.
pois.hours: Seasonal, roughly 7am-9pm in summer, shorter hours in shoulder season

pois.name: Al's Oasis
pois.note: Legendary South Dakota roadside stop since 1949 with a restaurant, gift shop, and grocery store right off I-90 at Chamberlain/Oacoma.
pois.nearTown: Oacoma, SD (across the river from Chamberlain)
pois.address: 1000 E South Dakota Hwy 16, Oacoma, SD 57365

pois.name: Phillips Avenue Diner
pois.note: Downtown Sioux Falls corner diner known for all-day breakfast and hand-crafted burgers in a vintage setting.
pois.address: 121 S Phillips Ave, Sioux Falls, SD 57104

pois.name: Minerva's Restaurant
pois.note: Sioux Falls dining landmark since 1977 on South Phillips Avenue, a solid choice for a proper sit-down dinner; closed Sundays.
pois.address: 301 S Phillips Ave, Sioux Falls, SD 57104

pois.name: Spearfish / Black Hills KOA Holiday
pois.note: Full-hookup RV park and tent camping just off US-14 on the edge of town, convenient base for exploring Spearfish Canyon.

pois.name: Spearfish City Campground
pois.note: Shaded municipal campground with full hookups along Spearfish Creek near D.C. Booth Historic Fish Hatchery, walkable to downtown.

pois.name: Sage Creek Campground
pois.note: Free, primitive, first-come first-served NPS campground on Sage Creek Rim Road — no water or electricity, but abundant bison and prairie dogs right at your campsite.
pois.hours: No reservations, no fee — first-come, first-served; access road can close after heavy rain

pois.name: Cedar Pass Campground
pois.note: The park's developed 96-site campground near Ben Reifel Visitor Center, with reservable group sites, restrooms, and ranger-talk amphitheater.
pois.hours: Open late March-mid-October; individual sites first-come, first-served

pois.name: Badlands / White River KOA Holiday
pois.note: Full-service KOA about 4 miles past Interior, a good developed alternative to Sage Creek's primitive sites.

pois.name: Oasis Campground (Al's Oasis)
pois.note: Full-hookup RV park attached to Al's Oasis with easy access off I-90 Exit 260.

pois.name: Sioux Falls KOA
pois.note: Full-hookup RV park near I-90/I-29 on the east side of Sioux Falls, a practical last night before heading into Minnesota.
pois.address: 1401 E Robur Dr, Sioux Falls, SD 57104

pois.name: Devils Tower National Monument
pois.note: America's first national monument, a 1,267-ft igneous rock tower sacred to Northern Plains tribes; visitor center, paved Tower Trail loop, and campground nearby.
pois.address: Devils Tower National Monument Rd, Devils Tower, WY 82714
pois.hours: Visitor center 9am-5pm daily; monument grounds open 24/7 (seasonal variation)

pois.name: Roughlock Falls Nature Area
pois.note: Easy boardwalk/trail to a scenic tiered waterfall on Little Spearfish Creek, reached via Forest Road 222 off the Scenic Byway near Savoy.
pois.hours: Open daily, daylight hours; no entrance fee

pois.name: Bridal Veil Falls
pois.note: 60-foot waterfall visible right from the Spearfish Canyon Scenic Byway (US-14A) with a small roadside pullout — no hike required.

pois.name: Pinnacles Overlook
pois.note: Sweeping sunset viewpoint at one of the highest points in the park's north unit, overlooking Sage Creek Wilderness and the gateway to Sage Creek Rim Road.

pois.name: Notch Trail
pois.note: Ladder-assisted scramble up a log ladder through a slot canyon to a cliff-edge notch overlooking the White River Valley — the park's most adventurous short hike.

pois.name: Cliff Shelf Nature Trail
pois.note: Easy half-mile boardwalk loop through a juniper 'slump' forest clinging to the Badlands Wall, wheelchair-friendly at the start.

pois.name: Castle Trail
pois.note: The park's longest maintained trail at 5+ miles one-way, crossing open mixed-grass prairie beneath jagged Badlands spires.

pois.name: Door Trail
pois.note: Short boardwalk-then-scramble hike through a literal 'door' in the Badlands Wall into an otherworldly eroded landscape.

pois.name: Big Badlands Overlook
pois.note: The first jaw-dropping view of the Badlands Wall for drivers entering from I-90's Interior/Badlands exit — a must-stop photo pullout.

pois.name: Yellow Mounds Overlook
pois.note: Vividly colored, fossilized ancient soil forming golden and lavender mounds — one of the most photographed stops on Badlands Loop Road.

pois.name: Falls Park
pois.note: The namesake waterfalls of the Big Sioux River in a 123-acre park right in Sioux Falls, free to visit with an observation tower and walking paths.
pois.address: 131 E Falls Park Dr, Sioux Falls, SD 57104

pois.name: Dignity of Earth and Sky
pois.note: 50-foot stainless-steel sculpture of an Indigenous woman by artist Dale Lamphere, perched on a bluff over the Missouri River at the Chamberlain I-90 rest area.

pois.name: Historic Bullock Hotel
pois.note: 1895 hotel built by Deadwood's first sheriff Seth Bullock, in the heart of downtown's historic gaming district; reputedly haunted, no on-site RV parking.

pois.name: Historic Franklin Hotel
pois.note: Landmark 1903 hotel on Main Street with an ornate lobby and on-site Deadwood Legends Steakhouse; a classic option for staying in old-town Deadwood.

pois.name: Best Western Plains Motel
pois.note: Reliable chain motel right in Wall, walkable to Wall Drug and a practical base before or after the Badlands.

pois.name: Sunshine Inn Motel
pois.note: Independent motel on Wall's Main Street, a simpler alternative to the chain options near Wall Drug.

pois.name: Cedar Pass Lodge
pois.note: The only in-park lodging in Badlands National Park — rustic cabins steps from the Badlands Wall, plus a restaurant and gift shop, open mid-April through mid-October.

pois.name: AmericInn by Wyndham Chamberlain Conference Center
pois.note: Chain hotel in Chamberlain near I-90, a convenient overnight stop between the Badlands and Sioux Falls.

pois.name: Hilton Garden Inn Sioux Falls Downtown
pois.note: Downtown Sioux Falls hotel overlooking the Big Sioux River, walking distance to Falls Park and the Phillips Avenue restaurant district.

pois.name: Monument Health Spearfish Hospital
pois.note: Full-service hospital with 24/7 emergency care serving the Spearfish/northern Black Hills area.

pois.name: Monument Health Rapid City Hospital
pois.note: The nearest full-service regional hospital and trauma center for the Wall/Badlands area, roughly an hour's drive northwest of Cedar Pass.

pois.name: Sanford USD Medical Center
pois.note: South Dakota's only verified Level I Trauma Center, with 24/7 emergency care in Sioux Falls.

pois.name: Avera McKennan Hospital & University Health Center
pois.note: Major Sioux Falls hospital with 24/7 emergency services, an alternative to Sanford on the south side of the city.
pois.address: 1325 S Cliff Ave, Sioux Falls, SD 57105

pois.name: Les Schwab Tire Center (Spearfish)
pois.note: Full tire sales, repair, and alignment shop — useful stop for Sprinter tire issues before heading into the Black Hills.

pois.name: Camping World of Sioux Falls Service Center
pois.note: Full RV service and repair center in Sioux Falls, the main RV-specific service hub at this end of the route.
pois.address: 1601 E Robur Dr, Sioux Falls, SD 57104

pois.name: Les Schwab Tire Center (E Arrowhead)
pois.note: Tire sales, repair, and alignment on the east side of Sioux Falls.
pois.address: 5800 E Arrowhead Pl, Sioux Falls, SD 57110

pois.name: Les Schwab Tire Center (W 61st Cir N)
pois.note: Tire sales, repair, and alignment on the west/southwest side of Sioux Falls.
pois.address: 4200 W 61st Cir N, Sioux Falls, SD 57107

pois.name: Les Schwab Tire Center (W Anchor Ln)
pois.note: Additional Sioux Falls tire and repair location on the south side of the city.
pois.address: 309 W Anchor Ln, Sioux Falls, SD 57108

pois.name: Bish's RV of Sioux Falls
pois.note: Full-service RV dealership and service center just south of Sioux Falls, good for RV-specific repairs and maintenance on a Sprinter-based rig.
pois.address: 2415 N Bakker Landing Ave, Tea, SD 57064

pois.name: American Creek Campground
pois.note: RV park and campground right in Chamberlain along American Creek, close to the Missouri River and downtown.

pois.name: Kennebec KOA Journey
pois.note: Closest KOA to Chamberlain, a straightforward I-90 Exit 235 stop for RV hookups and tent sites.

pois.name: Super 8 by Wyndham Chamberlain SD
pois.note: Budget chain motel right off I-90 Exit 263 in Chamberlain, a reliable overnight stop on the Missouri River crossing.

pois.name: Josiah's Coffeehouse, Cafe & Bakery
pois.note: Well-regarded downtown Sioux Falls cafe known for all-day breakfast and baked goods, near Falls Park and Phillips Avenue.

zones.label: Lake Superior North Shore — Minnesota
zones.blurb: From Duluth's harbor up the scenic North Shore of Lake Superior past waterfalls and a century-old lighthouse, then west along Wisconsin's Hwy 2 to the threshold of Michigan's Upper Peninsula — a long, well-serviced transition day between the prairie and the boreal UP.
tips: Duluth is the last major service hub (hospitals, tire shops, big grocery) before a long stretch of small towns — fuel up, restock, and handle any vehicle issues here.

Gooseberry Falls and Split Rock Lighthouse are extremely popular in fall color season; arrive early for parking, and note Split Rock's lighthouse tower itself typically closes for the season by mid-October.
MN-61 hugs the lake with frequent scenic pull-offs — budget extra time, and watch for deer at dawn/dusk the whole way to the UP.

safety.cellCoverage: Solid along MN-61 and US-2 through towns; short gaps in the state park corridors and on quieter stretches of US-2 in the western UP.
safety.nearestHospital: Duluth (Essentia St. Mary's / Aspirus St. Luke's) for the Minnesota leg; Ashland, WI or Ironwood, MI for the western stretch; Marquette, MI approaching the UP leg.
safety.note: Lake Superior water is cold year-round and undertows/rogue waves occur at exposed points like Palisade Head — stay back from unguarded cliff edges and wet rock.

pois.name: Holiday Stationstores (Johnstown Dr)
pois.note: 24-hour diesel and fuel stop with a convenience store, a reliable fill-up entering or leaving Duluth.

pois.name: Fuel stop on MN-61 (Duluth)
pois.note: Pay-at-pump station right on the MN-61 expressway as you head northeast out of Duluth toward the North Shore.

pois.name: Holiday Stationstores (Two Harbors)
pois.note: Main fuel stop right on Hwy 61 through Two Harbors, with 93 octane and a small gift shop.

pois.name: Silver Bay Hwy 61 gas station
pois.note: Fuel stop on Hwy 61 through Silver Bay, roughly midway between Split Rock and Palisade Head.

pois.name: Mariners Mobil
pois.note: In-town Mobil station on Outer Drive in Silver Bay, a backup if the Hwy 61 pumps are busy.

pois.name: Midland Services Cenex
pois.note: 24-hour pay-at-pump Cenex with a small grocery and liquor section in downtown Ashland.

pois.name: Circle K (E Cloverland Dr)
pois.note: 24/7 gas station on US-2 through Ironwood with regular, premium and diesel.

pois.name: Holiday Stationstores (Wakefield)
pois.note: Fuel stop on US-2 in Wakefield, between Ironwood and the drive toward Michigamme/Marquette.

pois.name: Meijer Express Gas Station
pois.note: Large fuel stop with all grades plus diesel on US-41 entering Marquette.

pois.name: Holiday gas station (US-41 W)
pois.note: Second reliable fuel option on US-41 through Marquette.

pois.name: Northern Waters Smokehaus
pois.note: Beloved Lake Superior smoked-fish deli in the DeWitt-Seitz Marketplace at Canal Park — smoked trout, lake trout jerky, and legendary sandwiches.

pois.name: Duluth Grill
pois.note: Scratch-made, farm-to-table breakfast and comfort food institution just off I-35/Hwy 61, a Diners Drive-Ins and Dives stop.

pois.name: Betty's Pies
pois.note: Iconic North Shore pie shop right on Hwy 61 north of Two Harbors — a quintessential road-trip stop, ships pies nationwide.

pois.name: New Scenic Cafe
pois.note: Well-regarded farm-to-table restaurant on Scenic Hwy 61 just north of Duluth, known for its lake views and seasonal menu.

pois.name: Grandma's Saloon & Grill
pois.note: Duluth's famous Canal Park restaurant tied to the Grandma's Marathon race, casual American fare with harbor views.

pois.name: Vanilla Bean Bakery & Cafe
pois.note: Local bakery-cafe on Hwy 61 just north of Two Harbors, popular breakfast and coffee stop.

pois.name: South Shore Brewery
pois.note: Long-running brewpub in downtown Ashland with a full kitchen — a good sit-down dinner stop off Hwy 2.

pois.name: Black Cat Coffeehouse
pois.note: Local coffeehouse and cafe in downtown Ashland, a reliable caffeine stop on the Hwy 2 leg.

pois.name: Don & GG's Food & Spirits
pois.note: Longtime local supper-club-style restaurant in Ironwood, a solid dinner stop before or after Van Riper.

pois.name: The Vierling Restaurant & Marquette Harbor Brewery
pois.note: Historic downtown Marquette restaurant and brewpub overlooking the harbor, a great end-of-day meal in the UP.

pois.name: Gooseberry Falls State Park Campground
pois.note: Popular drive-in campground steps from the park's famous waterfalls, with showers and RV-friendly sites; reserve ahead in fall color season.

pois.name: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park — Shipwreck Creek Campground
pois.note: 46 seasonal electric sites plus year-round walk-in/cart-in sites near the iconic lighthouse; a scenic overnight right on the shore.
pois.address: 3755 Split Rock Lighthouse Road, Two Harbors, MN 55616

pois.name: Jay Cooke State Park Campground
pois.note: Forested campground along the St. Louis River gorge just southwest of Duluth, a good option if starting the day early from the Duluth area.

pois.name: Van Riper State Park Campground
pois.note: 147-site modern campground on the western shore of Lake Michigamme — the natural overnight before pushing on to Marquette and the rest of the UP.

pois.name: Little Girl's Point County Park
pois.note: Lake Superior bluff-top campground and beach a short detour north of Ironwood — known for agate hunting and sunset views.

pois.name: Tourist Park Campground
pois.note: City-run campground along the Dead River on Marquette's north side, a convenient in-town base.

pois.name: Gooseberry Falls
pois.note: Five waterfalls cascading over ancient lava-flow rock right along the Gooseberry River — the North Shore's most-visited natural landmark.

pois.name: Split Rock Lighthouse
pois.note: Minnesota's most-photographed lighthouse, perched on a 130-foot cliff, built after the devastating 1905 Mataafa storm.

pois.name: Split Rock River Loop
pois.note: 4.3-mile loop along the Superior Hiking Trail through a scenic river gorge to a Lake Superior overlook; trailhead reached via a pedestrian tunnel under Hwy 61.

pois.name: Palisade Head
pois.note: 350-foot rhyolite cliff with panoramic Lake Superior views — drive to the top lot or hike a half-mile from the Hwy 61 pull-off.

pois.name: Shovel Point, Tettegouche State Park
pois.note: Dramatic lakeside cliff-top hike a few minutes north of Palisade Head, part of the same rugged volcanic shoreline.

pois.name: Enger Tower
pois.note: Five-story stone lookout tower on a hilltop park with sweeping views over Duluth's harbor and Lake Superior.

pois.name: Duluth Lakewalk
pois.note: Paved lakeside path along Duluth's Canal Park and harbor, an easy leg-stretcher with lighthouse and pier views.

pois.name: Brighton Beach
pois.note: Rocky Lake Superior beach and scenic drive just north of Duluth on Hwy 61, popular for agate hunting.

pois.name: Presque Isle Park
pois.note: Forested peninsula park on Lake Superior in Marquette with the volcanic 'Black Rocks' cliff-jumping spot and a scenic loop drive.

pois.name: Little Girl's Point Overlook
pois.note: High bluff over Lake Superior just north of Ironwood, one of the best sunset spots on the western Lake Superior shore.

pois.name: Canal Park Lodge
pois.note: Upscale, smoke-free hotel in the heart of Canal Park, walkable to the Lift Bridge and Lakewalk.

pois.name: Comfort Suites Canal Park
pois.note: All-suite hotel on the Lake Superior shore, a short walk from Canal Park's restaurants and the aquarium.

pois.name: The Suites Hotel at Waterfront Plaza
pois.note: Extended-stay all-suites hotel with kitchenettes, some with fireplaces and whirlpools, in Canal Park.

pois.name: Superior Shores Resort
pois.note: Lakefront resort just north of Two Harbors with an indoor pool, a solid base for exploring Gooseberry and Split Rock.

pois.name: AmericInn by Wyndham Ironwood
pois.note: Chain hotel right on US-2 through Ironwood with free breakfast, indoor pool and whirlpool.

pois.name: Indianhead Ironwood Motel
pois.note: Independent motel directly on US-2 about a mile from downtown Ironwood, a straightforward budget option.

pois.name: Econo Lodge Lakeside
pois.note: Budget chain hotel on US-41 south of downtown Marquette, close to Lake Superior.

pois.name: Holiday Inn Marquette
pois.note: Full-service hotel on US-41 West entering Marquette, a reliable overnight base for the UP leg.

pois.name: Essentia Health-St. Mary's Medical Center
pois.note: Level I adult / Level II pediatric trauma center with 24/7 emergency care — the major regional hospital for the Duluth area.

pois.name: Aspirus St. Luke's Hospital
pois.note: Second major Duluth hospital with a 24/7 emergency department, downtown near Essentia St. Mary's.

pois.name: Lake View Memorial Hospital
pois.note: Small community hospital with emergency care in Two Harbors, useful before the longer stretch up the shore.

pois.name: Memorial Medical Center
pois.note: 24-hour critical access hospital with an emergency department in Ashland, the main ER for the western Hwy 2 stretch.

pois.name: Aspirus Ironwood Hospital
pois.note: Emergency department serving Ironwood and the western UP, the last major hospital before the remote push toward Marquette.

pois.name: UP Health System – Marquette
pois.note: The largest regional hospital in the Upper Peninsula, with a full 24/7 emergency department.

pois.name: Firestone Complete Auto Care
pois.note: Full-service tire and mechanical shop on Miller Trunk Highway in Duluth — the last major repair stop before the North Shore and UP.

pois.name: Tires Plus Total Car Care
pois.note: Tire and general auto repair on West Central Entrance in Duluth, good for a pre-North-Shore vehicle check.

pois.name: NAPA Auto Parts (Duluth)
pois.note: Auto parts store with basic diagnostic help — useful for a quick fix or part before leaving Duluth's service hub behind.

pois.name: Discount Tire (Duluth)
pois.note: Tire sales and repair near the Miller Hill Mall commercial strip, an easy detour off I-35/Hwy 61 before the North Shore.

zones.label: Upper Peninsula & Pictured Rocks
zones.blurb: Marquette to Sault Ste. Marie along the Lake Superior shore — the sandstone cliffs of Pictured Rocks, twelve miles of wild beach, the amber cascades of Tahquamenon Falls, and the last U.S. night before the Canadian border.
tips: Twelvemile Beach Campground and the other Pictured Rocks drive-in campgrounds close for the season on October 15 — arriving October 16 means no water, no staffed toilets, and no reservations there; plan on a motel in Munising or Sault Ste. Marie instead.
H-58 between Munising and Grand Marais is mostly gravel and unlit — drive it in daylight, and fuel up before you start it since there's nothing but forest in between.
Miners Castle Road and the H-58 corridor have no cell service for long stretches — download offline maps and let someone know your route before you go.

safety.cellCoverage: Spotty to nonexistent along H-58 between Munising and Grand Marais, and patchy through the Tahquamenon Falls corridor; coverage returns reliably in Munising and Sault Ste. Marie.
safety.nearestHospital: Munising Memorial Hospital (Munising) or MyMichigan Medical Center Sault / War Memorial Hospital (Sault Ste. Marie)
safety.note: Pictured Rocks cliffs and overlooks have unfenced drop-offs — stay behind railings, especially in wind or rain. This is also bear country; store food properly at any campsite.

pois.name: Shell (E State Hwy M-28)
pois.note: Fuel stop with C-store and car wash on the main highway through town.
pois.address: 401 E State Highway M-28, Munising, MI 49862

pois.name: Hillside Gas Station
pois.note: Fuel and snacks on the west side of Munising along M-28.

pois.name: Circle K
pois.note: Convenience store and fuel near the downtown/M-28 junction.

pois.name: Bayshore Market & Gas
pois.note: The only fuel stop in Grand Marais — last gas before the long H-58 gravel stretch back toward Munising, or before continuing on to Tahquamenon. Fill up here regardless of which direction you're headed.

pois.name: Oasis Gas Station
pois.note: Second fuel option in Grand Marais, on Lake Avenue near the harbor.
pois.address: N14284 Lake Ave, Grand Marais, MI 49839

pois.name: Meijer Gas Station
pois.note: Large discounted fuel stop at the Meijer store on the west side of Marquette.

pois.name: Speedway (W Easterday Ave)
pois.note: Fuel stop on the main commercial strip heading into Sault Ste. Marie — last easy fill-up before the border crossing into Ontario.

pois.name: Shell (Business Spur I-75)
pois.note: Fuel near downtown Sault Ste. Marie, close to the Soo Locks and the international bridge approach.

pois.name: Marathon (M-28)
pois.note: Fuel stop on the western approach to Marquette.

pois.name: Driftwood Deli
pois.note: Downtown sandwich and salad shop sharing a building with ByGeorge Brewing — fresh, handcrafted, locally-inspired specials.

pois.name: Earl E Byrds
pois.note: Classic American diner in downtown Munising, popular for breakfast and lunch.

pois.name: Falling Rock Cafe and Bookstore
pois.note: Coffee, baked goods, and books in the heart of downtown Munising — good spot to fuel up before Pictured Rocks.

pois.name: The Fish Basket
pois.note: Local spot for Lake Superior whitefish and classic fried fish baskets.

pois.name: Miners Pasty Kitchen
pois.note: Traditional U.P. pasties — a regional staple and easy road food for the H-58 drive.

pois.name: The Dunes Saloon (Lake Superior Brewing Co.)
pois.note: Small-town brewpub since 1995 with house-brewed beer, whitefish tacos, pizzas, and homemade root beer; the social hub of Grand Marais at the end of H-58.
pois.address: N14283 Lake Ave, Grand Marais, MI 49839

pois.name: The Yooper Pasty Company
pois.note: Opened 2023, serving traditional Upper Peninsula pasties in Sault Ste. Marie.

pois.name: Lockview Restaurant
pois.note: Longtime family restaurant overlooking the Soo Locks — order a burger and watch the freighters lock through.

pois.name: Black Rock Bar & Grill
pois.note: Casual bar and grill in Sault Ste. Marie for a sit-down dinner on the last U.S. night.

pois.name: Twelvemile Beach Campground
pois.note: 36 NPS sites on a sandy bluff above Lake Superior, right on the beach; reservations-only via Recreation.gov. IMPORTANT: this campground's operating season runs May 15–October 15 — it closes for the year the day before an Oct 16 arrival, with water systems and toilets shut down. Treat this as unavailable and plan a motel instead.
pois.nearTown: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore (off H-58, between Munising and Grand Marais)

pois.name: Hurricane River Campground
pois.note: 21-site NPS campground on Lake Superior near the Au Sable Light Station trailhead; same May 15–Oct 15 season as Twelvemile Beach, so also closed by an Oct 16 visit.
pois.nearTown: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore (12 mi west of Grand Marais on H-58)

pois.name: Little Beaver Lake Campground
pois.note: Small 8-site NPS campground on an inland lake off H-58; same seasonal May 15–Oct 15 closure applies.

pois.name: Bay Furnace Campground
pois.note: Hiawatha National Forest campground on Lake Superior at the site of an 1870s iron-smelting furnace, just west of Munising near Christmas, MI — a fallback option closer to town.

pois.name: Rivermouth Campground, Tahquamenon Falls State Park
pois.note: Michigan DNR campground where the Tahquamenon River meets Lake Superior; modern sites with electric, open later into the fall than the NPS Pictured Rocks campgrounds. Reserve through Michigan DNR's reservation system.

pois.name: Lower Falls Campground, Tahquamenon Falls State Park
pois.note: Wooded DNR campground close enough to the Lower Falls to hear the rapids; a good base for exploring both the Upper and Lower Falls.

pois.name: Miners Castle
pois.note: The most famous formation in Pictured Rocks — a turreted sandstone outcrop with three viewing platforms (200–1,300 ft) overlooking Lake Superior. Trails open 24/7 year-round; the paved overlook path is an easy walk from the parking lot.
pois.nearTown: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, off Miners Castle Rd

pois.name: Miners Beach
pois.note: Dark, mineral-flecked sand beach reachable by a short trail down from Miners Castle (about 2 miles round trip) or its own parking area; a scenic, less-crowded stretch of Lake Superior shoreline.

pois.name: Munising Falls
pois.note: 50-foot waterfall a short, easy walk from the Munising Falls Visitor Center on the east edge of town — the classic first stop entering Pictured Rocks from the west.

pois.name: Twelvemile Beach
pois.note: One of the longest, wildest stretches of undeveloped sand beach on the Great Lakes — 12 miles of Lake Superior shoreline accessible from H-58 pullouts even when the campground itself is closed for the season.
pois.nearTown: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, off H-58

pois.name: Grand Sable Dunes / Log Slide Overlook
pois.note: Massive perched sand dunes rising 300+ feet above Lake Superior, where loggers once slid timber down to the lake — dramatic overlook just west of Grand Marais.

pois.name: Tahquamenon Falls — Upper Falls
pois.note: One of the largest waterfalls east of the Mississippi — over 200 feet wide and roughly 50 feet high, with a short paved path to the main overlook. The tannin-stained water runs amber, giving it the nickname 'root beer falls.'
pois.nearTown: Tahquamenon Falls State Park, Paradise, MI

pois.name: Tahquamenon Falls — Lower Falls
pois.note: A series of smaller cascades wrapping around a central island, four miles downstream from the Upper Falls; you can rent a rowboat to paddle out to the island.
pois.nearTown: Tahquamenon Falls State Park, Paradise, MI

pois.name: Munising Memorial Hospital
pois.note: Small critical-access hospital with 24-hour emergency room serving the Munising and Pictured Rocks area.

pois.name: War Memorial Hospital (MyMichigan Medical Center Sault)
pois.note: Full-service hospital with 24-hour ER — the last major U.S. medical facility before crossing into Ontario. Now part of MyMichigan Health but still commonly called War Memorial.
pois.address: 500 Osborn Blvd, Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783

pois.name: Comfort Inn & Suites Munising
pois.note: Lakefront hotel with Lake Superior and Grand Island views, walking distance to Munising, Tannery, and Memorial Falls — a solid fallback if Pictured Rocks camping is rained/closed out.

pois.name: Superior Motel & Suites
pois.note: Downtown Munising motel with kitchenette rooms, close to the visitor center.

pois.name: Alger Falls Motel
pois.note: Small independent motel just outside downtown Munising on M-28.

pois.name: Lockview Motel
pois.note: Family-run motel near the Soo Locks in Sault Ste. Marie — simple, central, and an easy walk to the locks and downtown.

pois.name: Holiday Inn Express Sault Ste. Marie
pois.note: Chain hotel on the main commercial strip, a reliable last-night option before the border crossing.

pois.name: Super 8 by Wyndham Sault Ste. Marie
pois.note: Budget chain motel option on the strip approaching downtown Sault Ste. Marie.

pois.name: Auto Center Pit Stop — Tire Shop
pois.note: Established 1999; general auto repair, tires, and routine maintenance. Last major service town before Canada.
pois.address: 500 W 3 Mile Rd, Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783

pois.name: U.P. Tire Incorporated
pois.note: Tire sales and repair serving Sault Ste. Marie.
pois.address: 1129 E Easterday Ave, Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783

pois.name: Quality Automotive Repair
pois.note: General auto repair shop serving Sault Ste. Marie and the last stretch of U.S. highway before the border.
